name: Jeremiah
sourceNote: Written freshly, thought for thought, from the oldest Hebrew, Greek, and Aramaic witnesses (the Masoretic Text with the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Septuagint, and the Samaritan Pentateuch). © 2026 Jose Santiago. All rights reserved.

verses.text: This book holds the words of Jeremiah,{a} son of Hilkiah.{b} He came from the family of priests who lived in Anathoth,{c} a town in the land of Benjamin.
Yahweh began speaking to Jeremiah during the thirteenth year of Josiah’s rule over Judah. Josiah{d} was Amon’s son.{e}

Yahweh kept speaking through the years when Josiah’s son Jehoiakim{f} ruled Judah. His words kept coming until Josiah’s other son Zedekiah{g} finished his eleventh year as king. That was the year the people of Jerusalem were taken away from their city, in the fifth month (July–August).{h}
This is how Yahweh’s message first reached me:

“Before I shaped you inside your mother, I already knew you.
Before you came into the world, I had set you apart.
I have named you a prophet for the nations.”

I replied, “Oh no, Lord Yahweh!{i} I have no idea how to speak in public.
I am only a boy.”

But Yahweh told me,
“Never say, ‘I am just a boy.’
Everywhere I send you, you must go.
Whatever I command, you must say.

Do not be afraid of what they look like or how they glare,
because I am with you to rescue you,” announces Yahweh.

Then Yahweh stretched out His hand and touched my mouth. Yahweh told me,
“Now My words are in your mouth.

This very day I put you in charge of nations and kingdoms.
Your task is to uproot and demolish,
to destroy and overturn,
and then to build up and plant.”
Yahweh’s word came to me once more. “Jeremiah, what is in front of you?” He asked. I answered, “I am looking at an almond branch.”{j}
“Good, you saw it right,” Yahweh said. “I am watching{k} over My word to make sure it happens.”
Yahweh’s word came to me a second time. “What is in front of you now?” He asked. I answered, “A kettle on the boil, with its mouth leaning this way from the north.”{l}
Then Yahweh told me, “Trouble will pour out from the north onto everyone who lives in this land.

Listen, I am calling every kingdom of the north,” announces Yahweh. “Their rulers will arrive. Every one of them will place a throne in the open space by Jerusalem’s gates. They will camp against its walls all around, and against all the towns of Judah.
Then I will announce My verdicts against My people for all their evil. They walked away from Me. They burned incense{m} to other gods. They bowed down to idols that their own hands had made.
So get your belt tight and get ready! Speak to them every word I give you. Do not tremble at their faces, or I will make you tremble in front of them.
This very day I make you a fortress city, an iron pillar, and a wall of bronze. You will face the entire land: the kings of Judah, its leaders, its priests, and its ordinary citizens.
They will fight you, but they will never defeat you, because I am with you to save you,” announces Yahweh.

notes.text: Jeremiah (Hebrew Yirmeyahu) probably means “Yahweh lifts up” or “Yahweh sets in place.” The meaning is uncertain.
Hilkiah means “Yahweh is my share.”
Anathoth was a town for priests, about 3 miles (5 km) northeast of Jerusalem. See Joshua 21:18.
Josiah probably means “Yahweh supports” or “Yahweh heals.” The meaning is uncertain.
This was about 627 BC.
Jehoiakim means “Yahweh sets up.”
Zedekiah means “Yahweh is right and fair.”
The Hebrew says “the fifth month,” Av. That was in 586 BC. The modern months are close but not exact, because Hebrew months followed the moon.
Hebrew Adonai Yahweh. The Septuagint says “O Lord, you who are ruler over all.”
In Hebrew the word for “almond tree” (shaqed) sounds like the word for “watching” (shoqed) in verse 12. The almond tree blooms first in the year, so it was called the “wide-awake tree.”
Hebrew shoqed. See the note at verse 11. The Septuagint says “I have watched over my words to make them happen.”
Or “tilted away from the north,” pouring toward the south.
Or “sent offerings up in smoke.”

verses.text: Yahweh’s message came to me again.{a}

He said, “Go and shout to Jerusalem,
This is what Yahweh says.
I remember how faithful{b} you were in your early years,
how you cared for Me like a young bride.
You walked behind Me in the wilderness,
across ground that no one had ever sown.

Israel was set apart for Yahweh,
the first and best part of His harvest.
Anyone who ate from it was guilty,
and trouble fell on them,” announces Yahweh.

Listen to Yahweh’s message, descendants of Jacob,
every family of Israel.

This is what Yahweh says:
“What did your fathers find wrong with Me,
that they moved so far from Me?
They ran after empty idols{c}
and turned empty themselves.

They never wondered, ‘Where is Yahweh?
He pulled us out of Egypt.
He guided us across the barren wilderness,
over a land of dry valleys and pits,
a land of drought and total darkness,
where nobody walks and nobody settles.’

I led you into a country of orchards{d}
to enjoy its fruit and its fine produce.
But when you got there, you polluted My land.
You made My own property repulsive.

The priests did not wonder, ‘Where is Yahweh?’
The men who handled the Law did not know Me.
The leaders{e} broke away from Me.
Prophets spoke their messages in Baal’s{f} name
and went after what cannot profit anyone.

So I will take you to court once more,” announces Yahweh.
“I will take your grandchildren to court too.

Sail west to the islands of Kittim{g} and look.
Send people east to Kedar{h} and think hard.
See if anything like this has ever happened.

Has any nation traded in its gods?
And those are no gods in the first place!
Yet My people have swapped their Glorious One{i}
for something useless.

Be shocked at this, sky!
Shake with horror and go empty,” announces Yahweh.

“My people have done two evil things.
They left Me, a spring of fresh flowing water.
Then they dug their own tanks in the ground,
cracked tanks that cannot hold any water.

“Is Israel a slave? Was he born into a servant’s house?
Then why has he been carried off as loot?

Young lions have roared at him.
They growled loudly.
They turned his land into a wasteland.
His towns are burned down, and nobody lives in them.

Even the men of Memphis{j} and Tahpanhes{k}
have scraped{l} the crown of your head.

Did you not bring this on yourself
when you left Yahweh your God,
even while He was leading you along the road?

So what do you gain from the road to Egypt,
drinking from the Nile’s waters?{m}
What do you gain from the road to Assyria,
drinking from the Euphrates?

Your own evil will teach you a lesson.
Your own turning away will prove you wrong.
Think about it and see how bitter and harmful it is
when you leave Yahweh your God
and have no respect for Me,”
announces the Lord, Yahweh of Armies.{n}

“A long time ago you snapped your yoke.
You tore off the ropes and said, ‘I will not serve you!’
Instead, on every high hill
and under every leafy tree
you lay down like a woman who sells herself.

I had planted you as a choice red vine,
grown from perfect seed.
How did you turn into a wild, sour plant
that does not look like My vine at all?

Even if you wash yourself with lye
and use a great deal of soap,
the stain of your guilt is still right here before Me,”
announces the Lord Yahweh.

“How can you say, ‘No stain is on me.
I never went after the Baals’?
Look at your path in the valley.{o}
Face what you have done.
You are a fast young she-camel
dashing in every direction,

or a wild donkey at home in the desert.
In her craving she sniffs the wind.
Who can turn her around when she is in heat?
The males that chase her do not have to work hard.
They find her when her season comes.

Do not wear your feet bare of shoes.
Do not let your throat go dry.
But you said, ‘It is hopeless!
I love strangers’ gods,
and I will keep running after them.’

“Just as a thief is humiliated once he is found out,
Israel’s family is humiliated,
along with its kings and officers,
its priests, and its prophets.

They tell a tree, ‘You are my father.’
They tell a rock, ‘You gave me life.’
They have faced away from me and not toward me.
Yet in times of disaster they plead,
‘Rise up and rescue us!’

Where are the gods you made for yourselves?
If they are able to rescue you in your time of disaster,
let them rise up now!
Judah, the number of your gods
matches the number of your towns.{p}

“Why do you argue with Me?
All of you have turned against Me,” announces Yahweh.

“I punished your children for nothing.
They would not take correction.
Your own sword ate up your prophets
like a lion that tears apart its prey.

You people of today, take in what Yahweh says!
Was I ever like a wilderness for Israel,
or like a land of heavy darkness?{q}
Why do My people claim, ‘We are free to wander.
We will not come back to you’?

Does a young woman forget her jewelry?
Does a bride forget her sash?
But My people have forgotten Me,
and I cannot count the days.

“You are so good at chasing after love!
Even women with bad names
can learn from your ways.

The blood of the innocent poor is found
even on the edges of your robes.
You never caught them digging into your home.{r}
Yet in spite of all this,

you say, ‘I have done nothing wrong.
His anger must have left me.’
But look, I will put you on trial
because you claim, ‘I have not sinned.’

Why do you run around so much,
switching your direction?
Egypt will shame you,
just as Assyria shamed you.

You will leave that place too
with your hands on your head.{s}
Yahweh has turned down the ones you trust,
and they will not help you succeed.”

notes.text: The Septuagint does not have verse 1 or the first words of verse 2. It begins, “And he said, This is what the Lord says.”
Hebrew chesed, which means loyal love or faithfulness to a promise.
Hebrew hevel, “breath” or “puff of air.” It is often used for idols. The word “worthless” in the next line is the same word as a verb.
Hebrew “a land of the Carmel,” meaning a land of gardens and orchards.
Hebrew “shepherds,” meaning rulers.
Baal means “lord” or “master.” He was the storm god of the Canaanites.
Kittim was first the city of Kition on Cyprus. Here it means the lands to the west.
Kedar was a tribe in the Arabian desert to the east. So the verse means to search from the west to the east.
Jewish tradition says scribes changed this from “my glory” to “their glory.”
Hebrew Noph, which is Memphis, an old capital of northern Egypt.
Tahpanhes was a fort in the eastern Nile delta. See 43:7–9.
Or “shaved” or “cracked.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
Hebrew “the waters of the Shihor,” a branch of the Nile or the Nile itself. The Septuagint says “Geon.” “The River” in the next line means the Euphrates.

Hebrew Adonai Yahweh Tseva’ot. “Yahweh of Armies” is the traditional “LORD of hosts.” It shows God as the commander of heavenly and earthly armies. The Septuagint often leaves out “of Armies.” Here it says “says the Lord your God.”
This was probably the Valley of Ben-Hinnom (see 7:31). The Septuagint says “the burial ground.”
The Septuagint adds, “and you sacrificed to Baal on as many streets as Jerusalem has.” Compare 11:13.
Or “a land of deep gloom.” The Hebrew word ma’peliah appears only here.
This means they were not burglars killed at night, which the Law allowed (Exodus 22:2).
Putting hands on the head showed sorrow and shame (2 Samuel 13:19).

verses.text:
“Imagine a man who sends his wife away,{a}
and she goes off
to be some other man’s wife.
Is he allowed to take her back again?
Would that not pollute the whole country?
But you have lived with many lovers.
Do you now dare to come back to Me?” announces Yahweh.

“Look up to the bare hilltops.{b}
Is there any place where nobody lay with you?
You sat by the roadsides waiting for your lovers,
like a desert traveler{c} waiting to rob someone.
You made the land unclean
with your unfaithful and wicked ways.

That is why the showers stopped
and the spring rains{d} never came.
Even so, you wore the hard face of a woman who sells herself.
You refused to be ashamed.

Only now you called to me,
‘Father! You have been my close friend ever since my youth.

Will you stay angry forever?
Will you hold a grudge to the end?’
That is what you say,
yet you do every evil thing you can.”

During the time of King Josiah, Yahweh spoke to me. He said, “Did you notice what disloyal Israel{e} has done? She climbed every tall hill and sat beneath every leafy tree. In every one of those places she was unfaithful.
After she had done all this, I thought, ‘She will return to Me.’ But she did not return. Her sister Judah, who was also disloyal, saw it happen.
I saw that Israel was unfaithful, so I sent her away. I even gave her divorce papers. Still her disloyal sister Judah was not afraid. She went out and was unfaithful too.
She took her unfaithfulness so lightly that she made the land unclean. She was unfaithful to Me with stones and with wood.
Even so, her disloyal sister Judah did not return to Me with all her heart. It was only a show,” announces Yahweh.
Then Yahweh said to me, “Unfaithful Israel has acted less guilty than disloyal Judah.

Go and shout this message toward the north:
‘Come back, unfaithful Israel,’ announces Yahweh.
‘I will not stare at you in anger.
I am loyal,’ announces Yahweh.
‘I will not stay angry forever.

Just admit that you are guilty.
You turned against Yahweh your God.
You gave yourself to strangers’ gods
under every leafy tree.
You did not listen to My voice,’ announces Yahweh.
“Return, you unfaithful children,” announces Yahweh, “because I am your master and husband.{f} I will pick you, one out of a town and two out of a family, and bring you to Zion.
I will give you shepherds who share My heart. They will lead you by teaching you what is wise and what is true.

You will become many and fill the land. At that time,” announces Yahweh, “no one will say, ‘Where is the Box of Yahweh’s Agreement?’ It will not cross anyone’s mind. Nobody will remember it or miss it, and nobody will build a new one.
In that time Jerusalem will be named ‘Yahweh’s Throne.’ Every nation will meet there to honor Yahweh’s name. They will stop following the stubborn desires of their evil hearts.
In those days Judah and Israel will walk side by side. Together they will leave the north and enter the land I gave your ancestors as their own.

“I had said to Myself,
‘I would love to count you among My sons!
I want to give you a pleasant land,
the finest property of any nation.’
I thought you would call Me ‘Father,’
and never stop following Me.

But a wife may leave her husband and break faith with him.
That is how you broke faith with Me, Israel,” announces Yahweh.

A voice is heard on the bare hills.
The people of Israel cry and beg.
They have gone down a crooked road.
They forgot Yahweh their God.

“Come back, unfaithful children.
I will cure your unfaithfulness.”
“Yes, we come to you,
for you are Yahweh our God.

The noise and shouting on the hills
were a lie.
Only in Yahweh our God
will Israel find rescue.

From the time we were young,
the shameful god{g} has eaten up
everything our ancestors worked for:
their flocks, their herds,
their sons, and their daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame.
Let humiliation wrap around us.
We sinned against Yahweh our God,
both we and our fathers,
from our young days right up to now.
We never obeyed Yahweh our God.”

notes.text: See Deuteronomy 24:1–4, which says a man could not take back a wife he had divorced if she married someone else.
Hebrew shefayim, bare hilltops where people worshiped false gods.
Hebrew “an Arab,” a desert traveler.
Hebrew malqosh, the spring rain in March and April.
“Israel” here means the northern kingdom, which Assyria destroyed in 722 BC.
Or “I am your owner.” The Hebrew word ba’al can mean “husband” or “master.” It is also the name of the god Baal.
Hebrew ha-bosheth, “the shame.” This is a way to speak of Baal without saying his name.

verses.text:
“Israel, if you really come back,” announces Yahweh,
“then come back to Me.
Throw your disgusting idols away from My sight
and stop wandering.

Then you can swear, ‘As surely as Yahweh lives,’
and mean it, with truth, fairness, and honesty.
The nations will bless each other in His name,
and they will take pride in Him.”

Yahweh speaks to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem:
“Break up the ground that has never been farmed.
Do not sow seed among thorn bushes.

Belong completely to Yahweh.
Cut away what covers your hearts,{a}
you men of Judah and you who live in Jerusalem.
Otherwise My anger will burst out like a fire,
and burn with no one able to stop it,
because of your wicked deeds.”

Announce this in Judah. Declare it in Jerusalem:
“Blow the trumpet{b} across the land!
Shout at the top of your voice:
‘Gather together!
Let us run to the walled cities!’

Raise the flag toward Zion.
Run for safety. Do not stop,
because I am bringing trouble from the north,
and it will be a terrible crash.”

A lion has come out of its hiding place.
A destroyer of nations has set out.
He has left home
to turn your land into a wasteland.
Your towns will be rubble with no one living there.

For this, put on mourning clothes of rough cloth.
Cry out in sorrow,
because Yahweh’s fierce anger
is still aimed at us.
“On that day,” announces Yahweh, “the king will lose heart, and so will the officials. The priests will be horrified. The prophets will stand there stunned.”
Then I said, “Oh, Lord Yahweh! You have badly deceived this people and Jerusalem. You promised, ‘Peace is yours,’ but now a sword is at our throats.”{c}

When that time comes, a message will go to this people and to Jerusalem:
“A scorching wind off the bare desert hills
is rushing toward My people.
It will not blow away husks or clean the grain.

This wind is too strong for that. It comes at My command.
Now I Myself will announce My verdicts against them.”

Look, he is coming like storm clouds.
His chariots are like a whirlwind.
His horses are faster than eagles.
How terrible for us! We are destroyed!

Jerusalem, clean out the wickedness from your heart
so that you can be saved.
For how much longer will harmful thoughts
be lodged within you?

Listen! A messenger is shouting from Dan.
He is bringing bad news from the hills of Ephraim.{d}

“Tell the nations! Announce it to Jerusalem:
Armies that surround cities{e} are coming from a faraway land.
They are roaring their battle cry against Judah’s towns.

They have circled her like men guarding a field,
because she has rebelled against Me,” announces Yahweh.

“Your own conduct and deeds
brought this to you.
Here is your punishment, and it is bitter!
It has cut deep into your heart.”

My stomach, my stomach!{f} I twist in pain.
The walls of my heart are shaking.
My heart pounds inside me.
I cannot be quiet.
I have heard the trumpet, my soul,
the shout of war.

Crash follows crash,
because the whole land is wrecked.
In one moment my tents are destroyed.
In one second my tent cloths are torn down.

How long will I have to see the flag
and listen to the trumpet?

“My people are foolish.
They have not come to know Me.
They are like silly children,
without any understanding.
They are skilled at doing wrong,
but doing right is beyond them.”

I gazed at the earth. It was a shapeless, empty mess.{g}
I gazed at the sky, and no light was in it.

I gazed at the mountains. They trembled,
and every hill swayed.

I gazed again. Nobody was there.
Every bird of the sky had flown off.

I gazed again. The garden country{h} was now a desert.
Every one of its towns lay crushed
because of Yahweh and His burning anger.

This is what Yahweh says:
“The entire country will turn into a wasteland,
but I will not wipe it out completely.

For this reason the earth will mourn,
and the sky above will turn dark.
I have said it and made up My mind.
I will not change it or turn back.”

Every town runs away
at the sound of riders and bowmen.
People slip into the bushes
and scramble up the rocks.
All the towns are abandoned,
and not one person stays in them.

And you, ruined city, what are you doing?
You put on red clothes.
You fasten on gold ornaments.
You paint your eyes with dark makeup.{i}
You dress up to look lovely, but it does no good.
The lovers you wanted turn on you.
They are looking for your life.

I hear a scream like a woman in labor,
the anguish of a mother with her first baby.
It is Zion’s daughter, struggling to breathe,
reaching out her hands.
“I am doomed!
My life is slipping away to murderers.”

notes.text: Hebrew “circumcise your hearts,” meaning to remove what blocks a heart from loving God. See Deuteronomy 10:16.
Hebrew shofar, a trumpet made from a ram’s horn.
Or “you have deceived them.” The Septuagint says that false prophets told the people this.
Dan was the far north of Israel. The hills of Ephraim were just north of Jerusalem. So the news came down the road from the north.
Or “watchers” or “besiegers.”
Hebrew “my bowels,” the place where deep feelings were felt.
Hebrew tohu va-vohu, the same words used in Genesis 1:2 for the earth before God shaped it.
Hebrew ha-karmel, a land of gardens and orchards.
Hebrew puk, a dark powder used on the eyes.

verses.text:
“Dash along Jerusalem’s streets and lanes.
Look carefully and ask yourselves.
Search her open squares.
Is there a single person
who does what is fair and wants the truth?
If there is, I will pardon the whole city.

They may say, ‘As surely as Yahweh lives.’
Still, their promise is a lie.”

Yahweh, your eyes are searching for honesty.
You hit your people, but they felt no pain.
You wore them down, but they would not learn.
They made their faces harder than stone.
They would not turn back.

Then I thought, “These are just poor people.
They act foolishly because they never learned
the way of Yahweh
or the rules of their God.

I will go to the powerful people
and talk to them.
Surely they know the way of Yahweh
and the rules of their God.”
But they too had snapped the yoke in two
and torn off the ropes.

So a lion from the forest strikes them down.
A wolf from the desert plains tears them apart.
A leopard crouches by their towns.
Whoever leaves will be ripped to shreds.
Their rebellion is huge,
and their turning away has happened over and over.

“Why would I pardon you?
Your sons have abandoned Me.
They swore oaths by things that are not gods at all.
I fed them until they were full, yet they were unfaithful in marriage.
They filled the houses of prostitutes.

They are like fat horses with strong appetites.
Each one calls out for the wife of the man next door.

Should I not punish them for this?” announces Yahweh.
“Should I not pay back a nation like this one?

“March through her rows of grapevines and wreck them,
yet leave some standing.
Pull off her branches,
because they are not Yahweh’s.

Both the house of Israel and the house of Judah
have broken faith with Me completely,” announces Yahweh.

They have lied about Yahweh.
They say, “He will not act.
No harm will touch us.
War and famine are things we will never see.

The prophets are nothing but wind.
God’s word is not in them.
May their threats fall on their own heads!”

So this is what Yahweh, the God of Armies, says:
“Because of what you said,
I will turn My words in your mouth into a flame,
and these people into firewood that it burns up.

Listen, people of Israel, I am bringing a nation from far away to attack you,” announces Yahweh.
“It is a strong and ancient nation.
You do not know its language,
and you cannot understand a word they say.

Their arrow holders are like open graves.
Every one of them is a strong fighter.

Invaders will consume your crops and food.
They will take your sons and daughters.
Your flocks and herds will be eaten.
Your vineyards and fig trees will be stripped.
The strong cities you rely on
will fall to their swords.
“Even then,” announces Yahweh, “I will not completely destroy you.

When your people ask, ‘Why did Yahweh our God do all this to us?’ tell them, ‘As you left Him and worshiped foreign gods in your own land, you will now work for outsiders in a land that is not yours.’

“Announce this to the family of Jacob.
Spread the word in Judah:

‘Hear this, you silly people without understanding.
Eyes are on your faces, yet you cannot see.
Ears are on your heads, yet you cannot hear.

Do you not respect Me?’ announces Yahweh.
‘Do you not shake with fear in front of Me?
I set sand as the border for the sea.
It is a limit that lasts forever, and the waves cannot cross it.

But these people have a stubborn, rebel heart.
They have turned aside and walked away.

They never think,
“Let us honor Yahweh our God.
He gives us rain at the right time,
in the fall and in the spring,
and He keeps the harvest weeks safe for us.”{a}

Your wrong choices have kept the rain away.
Your sins have blocked good things from reaching you.

There are evil men among My people.
They hide like bird hunters lying low.
They set traps
and catch people.

Like a cage packed with birds,
their homes are packed with cheating.
That is how they got big and wealthy.

They have grown fat and shiny.
Their evil deeds have no limit.
They refuse to defend orphans in court so they can win.
They do not stand up for the rights of poor people.

Should I not punish them for this?’ announces Yahweh.
‘Should I not pay back a nation like this one?’

“Something horrible and appalling
is going on in this land.

The prophets announce lies.
The priests take charge for themselves.
My people enjoy it that way.
But when it is all over, what will you do?”

notes.text: Hebrew yoreh and malqosh, the fall rain (October–November) and the spring rain (March–April). “Harvest weeks” are the seven weeks between Passover and the Feast of Weeks.

verses.text:
I will wipe out Zion’s daughter,
who is so lovely and gentle.{c}

Shepherds with their flocks will march against her.
They will set up camp on every side of her.
Each one will let his animals eat his own patch.

They will say, ‘Get ready to fight her!{d}
Get up! We will attack at noon!’
Then they cry, ‘How awful for us! The day is fading,
and the evening shadows are growing long.’

Then they say, ‘Get up! We will attack at night
and knock down her strong towers.’”

This is what Yahweh of Armies says:
“Chop down her trees.
Heap up a siege ramp of earth against Jerusalem.
She is the city I must punish.
Oppression fills her inside from edge to edge.

A well keeps its water fresh.
In the same way she keeps her evil fresh.
Violence and ruin are the sounds heard inside her.
I always see sickness and wounds.

Be warned, Jerusalem,
or My heart will pull away from you.
I will make you a wasteland,
a country where nobody lives.”

This is what Yahweh of Armies says:
“Glean the survivors of Israel
the way you glean a vine.
Run your hand over the branches again,
as a grape gatherer does.”

Who can I speak to? Who will listen to my warning?
Look, their ears are shut,
and they cannot pay attention.
Yahweh’s word is something they laugh at.
They find no joy in it.

But I am filled with Yahweh’s anger.
I am tired of holding it back.
“Pour it out on the children playing in the street
and on the young men gathered together.
Husband and wife will both be caught,
and so will old people who have lived many years.

Their houses will go to other owners,
along with their fields and their wives.
I will reach out My hand
against everyone who lives in this land,” announces Yahweh.

“From the least important to the most important,
everyone is greedy for money they did not earn.
Prophets and priests alike
all tell lies.

They treat My people’s broken heart as if it were a scratch.
They say, ‘Peace, peace!’
when there is no peace at all.

Were they embarrassed by the disgusting things they did?
No, they were not ashamed in the least.
They never even learned how to blush.
So they will fall with everyone else who falls.
When I come to punish them, they will crash to the ground,” says Yahweh.

This is what Yahweh says:
“Stand where the roads meet and look.
Ask where the old paths are.
Ask where the good road is, and walk along it.
Then your souls will find rest.
But they said, ‘We will not walk there.’

I placed guards over you and said,
‘Listen for the sound of the trumpet.’
But they said, ‘We will not listen.’

So listen, nations.
Learn, crowd of people, what will happen to them.

Hear this, earth.
Look, I am bringing ruin to these people.
It is the result of their own plans,
for they have ignored what I said
and thrown out My teaching.

Incense brought from Sheba means nothing to Me,
and neither does sweet spice from a distant land.
Your burnt offerings do not please Me.
Your sacrifices do not make Me happy.”

So this is what Yahweh says:
“Look, I will lay down blocks for these people to trip on.
Parents and children will fall over them together.
Neighbor and friend will die.”

This is what Yahweh says:
“Watch! A people is coming from the northern country.
A mighty nation is waking up
in the farthest corners of the earth.

They hold bows and spears.
They are savage and have no pity.
They roar like the sea.
They ride horses,
lined up like soldiers for battle
against you, daughter of Zion.”

We have heard the report about them.
Our hands hang limp.
Agony has seized us,
like labor pains.

Stay out of the fields.
Stay off the roads.
An enemy with a sword is out there,
and fear surrounds us.{e}

My dear people, put on rough cloth for mourning
and roll in the ashes.
Cry out with the deepest sorrow
of a parent who has lost an only son,
because the destroyer will come on us
in a flash.

“I have made you a tester of metal{f} among My people,
so you can look at how they live
and judge their ways.

All of them are stubborn rebels.
They go around spreading gossip.
They are hard as bronze and iron.
Every one of them acts in a rotten way.

The bellows blast hot air.
The fire burns the lead away.{g}
The refiner keeps working, but it does no good,
because the evil is not removed.

People call them ‘rejected silver,’
because Yahweh has rejected them.”

notes.text: Tekoa was a town about 10 miles (16 km) south of Jerusalem. Its name sounds like the Hebrew word for “blow” (tiq’u).
Beth Hakkerem means “house of the vineyard.” It was probably Ramat Rachel, between Jerusalem and Bethlehem.
Or “I will cut off Zion’s daughter, a lovely pasture.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
Hebrew “make holy war on her,” because wars began with religious rites.
Hebrew magor missaviv, “terror on every side.” Jeremiah uses this phrase often. See 20:3, 10; 46:5; 49:29.
Or “a fortress.” Hebrew mivtsar. The picture is of refining silver from ore, with lead used to carry off the poor metal.
The Hebrew can also be read “the lead is burned up by the fire.” Another reading is “by their fire.”

verses.text: Yahweh gave Jeremiah a message.{a}
He said, “Stand at the gate of Yahweh’s Temple and shout this out: ‘Hear Yahweh’s message, everyone from Judah who enters these gates to worship Him.
Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, declares: Fix your ways and your deeds, and then you may remain{b} in this place.
Stop trusting in the false slogan: “The Temple of Yahweh! The Temple of Yahweh! The Temple of Yahweh is here!”{c}
Only if you truly change how you live and what you do, and only if you are fair to each other in every court case,
and only if you stop mistreating outsiders, orphans, and widows, stop killing innocent people here, and stop chasing other gods that will ruin you,
then I will let you live here, in the land I gave to your ancestors as theirs forever.
“‘But look at you. You trust in lies that will not help you.
Do you think you can steal, murder, break your marriage promises, tell lies under oath, and burn incense to Baal, then go after other gods you never knew,
and then walk into this house that has My name on it, stand before Me, and say, “We are safe”? You say that and then go right back to all these disgusting things!
Has this house, which carries My name, become a robbers’ hideout in your opinion? I have been watching it all,’ announces Yahweh.
“‘Go to My old home at Shiloh,{d} where I first set up a place for My name. Look at what I did to it, because My people Israel were so wicked.
You have done all these things,’ announces Yahweh. ‘I spoke to you again and again, starting early each day, but you would not listen. I called, but you did not answer.
So the house with My name on it, the house you trust, will get the same treatment Shiloh got. This will happen also to the land that I gave to you and your ancestors.
I will throw you out from where I can see you, as I threw out all your relatives, all the descendants of Ephraim.’
“Jeremiah, do not pray for these people. Do not cry out or plead for them. Do not beg Me, because I will not listen to you.
Do you not see what they are doing in Judah’s towns and on Jerusalem’s streets?
The children gather wood. The fathers start the fires. The women knead dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven.{e} They pour out drinks for other gods to make Me angry.
Am I the one they are hurting?” announces Yahweh. “No, they harm themselves, and their own faces turn red with shame.”

This is the message of the Lord Yahweh: “My anger and rage will pour out on this place. It will fall on people and animals, on field trees, and on the land’s crops. It will burn, and nobody will put it out.”
The Lord Yahweh of Armies, God of Israel, announces: “Go ahead, pile your burnt offerings on top of your other sacrifices, and eat the meat yourselves!{f}
When I led your ancestors out of Egypt, I never gave them any command or word about burnt offerings and sacrifices.
My command to them was this: ‘Obey Me. Then I will be your God, and you will be My people. Walk in every way I order, so that life goes well for you.’
But they would not obey or even pay attention. They followed their own plans and the stubbornness of their evil hearts. They went backward, not forward.
From the day your ancestors left Egypt right up to today, I kept sending you My servants the prophets, day after day, rising early to send them.
But the people ignored Me and would not pay attention. They were stiff-necked. They did even worse things than their ancestors.
“You will give them this whole message, yet they will not listen. You will shout to them, yet they will give you no reply.{g}
So tell them, ‘This is the nation that would not obey Yahweh its God and would not accept correction. Truth has died. It has disappeared from their mouths.’

“Cut off your hair{h} and throw it away.
Cry out a sad song on the bare hills,
because Yahweh has turned away from the people
who made Him furious, and He has left them.”
“The people of Judah have done evil in My sight,” announces Yahweh. “They set up their disgusting idols in the house that has My name on it and made it unclean.
They built the worship places of Topheth{i} in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom{j} and burned their sons and daughters in the fire there. I never ordered this. It never even entered My mind.

So listen, the days are coming,” announces Yahweh, “when nobody will use the names Topheth or Ben-Hinnom for it. Its name will be the Valley of Killing, since graves will fill Topheth until there is no room left.
Birds and wild animals will eat the corpses of these people, and nobody will scare them away.
I will end the sounds of joy and gladness in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, the voices of the groom and the bride, because the land will become a wasteland.”

notes.text: The Septuagint does not have verse 1 or the first half of verse 2. It begins, “Hear the word of the Lord, all Judah.” The same sermon is told again in chapter 26.
Or, with different vowels, “and I will stay with you.” The same applies in verse 7.
The Septuagint says the phrase twice: “It is the Temple of the Lord, the Temple of the Lord.”
Shiloh was where the sacred tent stood in the days of Eli (1 Samuel 1–4). It was apparently destroyed after the Philistines captured the Box of the Agreement.
She was probably Ishtar, the Mesopotamian goddess of love and war. See also 44:17–25. The Septuagint says “to the army of the sky.”
The burnt offerings were burned completely. God was telling them to eat even those, because he no longer valued them.
The Septuagint has only the first words of this verse: “So you will speak this word to them.”
Hebrew “your crown,” a sign of mourning. The words are spoken to Jerusalem as a woman.
Topheth was the place in the valley where children were burned as offerings. The name may mean “fireplace,” or it may be written with the vowels of boshet, “shame.”
Ben-Hinnom means “son of Hinnom.” It was the valley south and west of Jerusalem. Its later name, Gehinnom, led to the word “Gehenna.”

verses.text: “At that time,” announces Yahweh, “enemies will dig up the bones of Judah’s kings, officials, priests, prophets, and the people of Jerusalem from their graves.

They will spread them out under the sun, the moon, and the stars of the sky. Those were the things the people loved, served, followed, asked for advice, and bowed down to. Nobody will pick up the bones or bury them. They will become like animal waste lying on the soil.
All who survive from this evil family, wherever I have scattered them, will wish to die rather than live,” announces Yahweh of Armies.

“Tell them, ‘This is what Yahweh says:
When people fall, do they not stand up again?
When someone wanders off, do they not turn around?

So why do these people, Jerusalem’s people,
keep walking away without end?
They cling to lies.
They will not come back.

I listened closely,
but what they say is not right.
No one is sorry for his evil.
No one asks, “What have I done?”
Each one runs his own way,
like a horse charging into battle.

Even the stork in the sky
knows when to migrate.
The dove, the swift,{a} and the crane
know when to return.
But My people do not know
what Yahweh requires.

“‘How can you claim, “We are wise.
Yahweh’s Law is ours”?
In fact, the scribes’ false pens
have made it say something false.

The wise men are embarrassed.
They are terrified and trapped.
They have turned down Yahweh’s word,
so what wisdom do they have?

Their wives will be given away to other men,
and their fields to new owners.
From the lowest to the highest,
everyone is hungry for unfair profit.
Prophets and priests alike
all tell lies.

Were they ashamed of the horrible things they did?
No, they felt no shame at all.
They never learned to blush.
So they will drop with those who are dropping.
When I punish them, they will fall,’ says Yahweh.

‘I will gather them up for good,’{c} announces Yahweh.
‘No grapes are on the vine.
No figs are on the fig tree.
Even the leaves are dried up.
Whatever I gave them will pass away from them.’”{d}

Why do we just sit here?
Come together! Let us run to the walled cities
and perish there.
Yahweh our God has doomed us.
He has made us drink bitter poison water,{e}
because we sinned against Yahweh.

We wanted peace, yet nothing good arrived.
We wanted a season of healing, but fear arrived instead.

Enemy horses snort, and the sound reaches us from Dan.
When their strong stallions neigh,
the whole land shakes.
They have come to swallow the land and all that is in it,
the city and its people.

“Look, I am sending snakes among you,
poisonous snakes that nobody can charm.
They will bite you,” announces Yahweh.

My sadness cannot be cured.{f}
My heart is sick inside me.

Listen! My people are crying out
from a faraway country:
“Is Yahweh not in Zion?
Is her King not there?”
“Why did they anger Me with their carved idols
and their worthless foreign gods?”

“Harvest is past. Summer is over.
And still we are not rescued.”

I am crushed because my people are crushed.
I am in mourning. Horror has gripped me.

Is there no healing sap{g} in Gilead?
Is there no doctor there?
Then why has my people’s health
not been restored?{h}

notes.text: The Hebrew names the turtledove, the swift, and the crane. Some of these bird names are uncertain.
“All is well” is the Hebrew word shalom, “peace.”
The Hebrew of verse 13 is very hard to read, and its meaning is uncertain.
The last line of the Hebrew is very hard to translate. Ancient versions read it in different ways.
The Hebrew word may mean “poison” or “bitter water.”
The Hebrew of this verse is hard, and its meaning is uncertain.
The Hebrew word is tsori, probably a healing resin or balm from Gilead.
The Hebrew says “gone up,” like new flesh growing over a healed wound.

verses.text:
Oh, that my head held a lake of water
and my eyes ran like a spring of tears!
Day and night I would weep
over the dead among my people!{a}

I wish I had a hut in the desert,
a place for travelers to sleep.
Then I could leave my people
and go far away from them!
All of them are unfaithful,
a gang of cheats.

They bend their tongues like bows to shoot lies.
Lies, not truth, have taken over the land.
They go from one evil to the next,
and they do not know Me, announces Yahweh.

Be on guard against your friends.
Do not trust any brother.
Every brother is a cheat,{b}
and every friend spreads gossip.

Everyone fools his neighbor,
and nobody speaks honestly.
Their tongues have learned to lie.
They exhaust themselves doing wrong.

You live surrounded by lies.
Because of lies they refuse to know Me, announces Yahweh.

This is the message of Yahweh of Armies:
“I am about to melt them down and test them.
What other choice do I have with My people?

Their tongue is a deadly arrow.
It shoots out lies.
With his mouth, each one says “Peace” to his neighbor,
but in his heart he sets a trap.

Should I not punish them for this?” announces Yahweh.
“Should I not pay back a nation like this?”

I will weep and wail over the mountains.
I will chant a sad song over the desert pastures,
because they are burned dry, and no one travels through.
The sound of cattle is gone.
The birds and the animals
have run away.

“I will turn Jerusalem into a pile of stones,
a den for wild dogs.
I will make Judah’s towns a wasteland
where nobody lives.”
Who is wise enough to understand this? Who has heard it from Yahweh and can explain it? Why is the land ruined and dried up like the desert, so that no one goes through it?
Yahweh answered, “It is because they left the teaching I gave them. They did not obey Me or follow it.
They followed the stubborn desires of their own hearts. They went after the Baals, just as their ancestors taught them.
So Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I will feed these people bitter weeds and give them poison water to drink.
I will spread them out among nations unknown to them and to their ancestors. I will send a sword after them until I have finished them off.”

This is what Yahweh of Armies says:
“Think about it. Summon the women who are paid to mourn.
Send for the ones who are most skilled.

Let them come quickly and sing a sad song for us,
until tears pour from our eyes
and water runs down our eyelids.

A loud cry rises from Zion:
‘We are ruined!
We are so ashamed!
We have to abandon our land,
because our homes are torn down.’”

Women, hear Yahweh’s message.
Open your ears to what His mouth says.
Teach your daughters a sad song.
Teach each neighbor a funeral song.

Death has climbed in through our windows.
It has entered our fortresses.
It is cutting down children playing in the street
and young men in the city squares.

Say this: “Yahweh announces,
‘Dead bodies will lie
like dung in the open field,
like grain left behind by the reaper,
with no one to pick them up.’”

This is what Yahweh says:
“Wise people should not brag about their wisdom.
Strong people should not brag about their strength.
Rich people should not brag about their money.

If anyone wants to brag, they should brag about this:
that they have wisdom and know Me,
that I am Yahweh, who shows faithful love,
fairness, and right living on earth.
These are the things I enjoy,” announces Yahweh.
“Look, days are coming,” announces Yahweh, “when I will punish all who are circumcised only in their bodies:

Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who cut their hair at the temples,{c} who live in the desert. All these nations are uncircumcised, and the whole nation of Israel is uncircumcised in the heart.”

notes.text: In Hebrew Bibles this verse is 8:23, and chapter 9 begins at verse 2.
The Hebrew word for “cheat” (aqov) sounds like the name Jacob (Yaaqov).
The Hebrew says “who clip the corners of their hair.” Some desert peoples cut their hair at the temples.

verses.text: Israel’s people, listen to what Yahweh tells you.

Yahweh says:
“Do not learn the habits of the nations.
Do not be afraid of strange signs in the sky,
even though the nations are afraid of them.

What those peoples practice is empty.
Someone cuts a tree down in the forest.
A woodworker shapes it with his tool.

They cover it with silver and gold.
They nail it down with hammers
so it will stay upright.

Those idols are like straw men set up in a melon patch.{a}
They cannot speak.
They must be lifted and hauled around,
since they cannot walk.
Never fear them.
Harm is beyond their power,
and so is help.”

Yahweh,{b} nobody compares to you.
You are great, and your name carries great power.

Who would not show you respect, King over every nation?
Respect is what you are owed.
Among every wise person from the nations,
and in all of their kingdoms,
there is nobody like you.

They are all senseless and foolish.
What an idol teaches is only a piece of wood.

Beaten silver is shipped in from Tarshish,
and gold from Uphaz.{c}
A skilled worker and a goldsmith make the idol.
Then it is dressed in blue and purple cloth.
All of it is the work of clever craftsmen.

But Yahweh is the real God.
He is the God who lives, and He is King forever.
When His anger burns, the earth shakes.
No nation can hold up under His rage.
Tell them this:{d} “The gods who did not make the sky and the earth will disappear from the earth and from under the sky.”

God made the earth with His power.
He set up the world with His wisdom.
With His understanding He spread out the sky.

When He speaks, the waters in the sky thunder.
From the ends of the earth He lifts up clouds.
He makes lightning for the rainstorm,
and He sends wind from His storerooms.

Everyone is foolish and has no knowledge.
Every goldsmith is put to shame by the idol he made,
because his metal figures are fake,
and there is no breath in them.

They are worthless, ridiculous things.
On the day they are judged, they will be wiped out.

The One Who Is Jacob’s Share{e} is nothing like them.
He formed all things,
and Israel is the tribe He chose to be His own.
His name is Yahweh of Armies.

Pick up your bundle from the ground,
you who are trapped inside a city under attack.

Yahweh says:
“Look, this time I will throw the people of the land out like stones from a sling.
I will bring them pain
so that they will learn.”{f}

How I hurt from my broken body!
My wound is deep.
I told myself, “This is just a sickness,
and I will have to bear it.”

My tent is destroyed.
All of its ropes are snapped.
My children have gone away from me
and are no more.
Nobody is left to set up my tent
or hang my cloths in place.

The shepherds are senseless.
They do not ask Yahweh for guidance.
So they have not done well,
and their whole flock is scattered.

Listen! A report is coming. Look, it is here!
A loud crash is coming from the northern country.
It will turn the towns of Judah into ruins,
a place where wild dogs live.

Yahweh, I know that people do not run their own lives.
Nobody can steer his own steps as he walks.

Correct me, Yahweh, but do it gently.
Do not correct me in anger, or I will be nothing.

Pour out Your fury on the nations that never knew You,
and on the clans that never prayed in Your name.
They have swallowed up Jacob.
They have eaten him and finished him off,
and they have ruined his home.

notes.text: Or “like pillars in a cucumber field.” The word is uncertain.
Some ancient Septuagint copies leave out verses 6–8 and 10.
Uphaz is a place known for fine gold. Its location is unknown. Some copies say “Ophir.”
Verse 11 is written in Aramaic, the everyday language of the Near East, not in Hebrew.
Jacob’s Share is a name for God. It means that Yahweh is what Jacob’s family received, instead of land. Compare Psalm 16:5.
The Hebrew of the last line is hard to read. It may mean “so that they will find it.”

verses.text: This is a message Jeremiah received from Yahweh.
“Listen to the words of this agreement.{a} Tell them to the men of Judah and to the people living in Jerusalem.
Say to them, ‘Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: A curse falls on anyone who ignores the words of this agreement.

I gave these terms to your ancestors the day I led them out of Egypt, out of that furnace for melting iron. I told them, “Obey Me and do everything I order. Then you will be My people, and I will be your God.”
I did this to keep the oath I swore to your ancestors. I swore to give them a land rich with milk and honey, which is the land you have today.’” I answered, “Amen,{b} Yahweh. Let it be so.”
Then Yahweh said to me, “Call out these words in Judah’s towns and in Jerusalem’s streets. Say, ‘Hear what this agreement requires, and put it into practice.
From the day I brought your ancestors out of Egypt until today, I warned them over and over, rising early to do it. I said, Obey Me.{c}

They did not listen or pay attention. Each one did what his stubborn, evil heart wanted. So every curse written in this agreement fell on them, because they had ignored the commands I gave them to follow.’”
Yahweh said to me, “I have discovered a secret plot among the men of Judah and the citizens of Jerusalem.

They have gone back to the faults of their forefathers, who would not hear My words. They too have run after other gods to serve them. Both Israel’s family and Judah’s family have shattered the promise I made with their forefathers.
So here is what Yahweh says: I am about to send disaster on them, and they will not escape it. They will cry out to Me, but I will not listen.
Then Judah’s towns and Jerusalem’s citizens will run to the gods they offer incense to and beg for help. But those gods will never rescue them when disaster strikes.
Judah, the number of your gods equals the number of your towns. The altars you built to burn incense to the Shame{d} equal the number of Jerusalem’s streets. They are altars to Baal.
“Jeremiah, do not pray for these people. Do not offer any cry or request for them. I will refuse to hear them when they call out to Me because of their trouble.

What is My beloved doing in My house
after carrying out so many evil plans?
Can promises{e} and sacred meat
take your disaster away?
Then you could celebrate.

Yahweh once called you a green olive tree,
lovely, with fine fruit.
But with a roar like a great storm,
He has set it on fire.
Its branches are broken.{f}
Yahweh of Armies planted you, and He has declared that disaster is coming to you. The reason is the evil done by Israel’s family and Judah’s family, who made Me angry by burning incense to Baal.”

Yahweh showed me, so I knew.
He let me see what they were doing.

I was like a tame lamb
being led to slaughter.
I had no idea that plots were being made against me.
They said, “Let us ruin the tree while it is full of sap!{g}
Let us wipe him off the earth of the living,
so no one remembers his name.”

But You, Yahweh of Armies, are a fair judge.
You test the deepest feelings{h} and thoughts.
Let me watch You pay them back,
because I have left my case in Your hands.
So this is Yahweh’s word about the men of Anathoth. They want to kill you, and they say, “Do not prophesy in Yahweh’s name, or we will kill you.”
Yahweh of Armies says: “Look, I will punish them. Their young men will die by the sword. Their sons and daughters will starve.
Not one of them will be left, because the year of their punishment will bring disaster to the men of Anathoth.”

notes.text: Hebrew berit, usually “covenant.” It means a binding promise between God and his people.
“Amen” is Hebrew for “so be it” or “truly.”
Some copies of the Septuagint do not have the last words of this verse.
Hebrew ha-bosheth, “the Shame.” This was a way to avoid saying the name Baal.
Or “vows.” Some Hebrew copies read “the many” instead.
The last two lines are uncertain in Hebrew. Some read “its branches will be good for nothing.”
Hebrew “destroy the tree with its food.” The meaning is uncertain.
Hebrew “kidneys,” the place where deep feelings were thought to be.

verses.text:
Yahweh, You are right every time
when I bring a complaint to You.
Still, I need to ask You about justice:
Why do wicked people do so well?
Why are traitors so comfortable?

You set them in the ground, and roots go down.
They grow tall and produce fruit.
Your name is always in their speech,
yet You are far from their hearts.

But You, Yahweh, know me.
You see me and test my heart toward You.
Drag them away like sheep for the butcher.
Reserve them for the day they are killed.

How long will the land dry up and mourn?
The grass in every field has withered.
Because of the evil of those living there,
animals and birds are dying.
Yet the people say, “God does not see how our lives turn out.”

Even your own relatives,
your father’s family,
have betrayed you.
They shout loudly behind your back.
Never rely on them,
even if their words sound kind.

“I have left My house.
I have given up My own property.
I have handed the one I love most
over to her enemies.

To Me, My inheritance has become
a lion in the forest.
She has roared at Me.
So I hate her.

Is My own people like a spotted bird of prey?{c}
Are other birds of prey circling her?
Go and collect every wild animal.
Bring them in to feast.

Many shepherds ruined My vineyard.
They trampled My field.
They changed My lovely field
into a bare desert.

They made it a wasteland.
It lies dry and sad in front of Me.
The whole land is wrecked,
and nobody cares.

Destroyers have come over
the bare hills of the desert,
because Yahweh’s sword is eating
from one end of the land to the other.
Nobody is safe.

The people planted wheat but harvested thorns.
They wore themselves out and got nothing.
You will be ashamed{d} of your harvests
because of Yahweh’s fierce anger.”

Here is what Yahweh says about all My evil neighbors who attack the land I gave My people Israel as their own: “Look, I will tear them out of their land. I will also tear Judah’s people out from among them.
But once I have torn them out, I will have pity on them again. Each person will go home to his own property and his own country.
If they carefully learn the ways of My people and swear in My name, ‘As surely as Yahweh lives,’ just as they once taught My people to swear by Baal, then they will be established among My people.
But a nation that will not obey I will uproot and destroy,” announces Yahweh.

notes.text: Or “if you feel safe only in a peaceful land.” The Hebrew is hard to read.
The Jordan River had thick brush and tall grass along its banks, where lions hid.
Or “a hyena’s den.” The Hebrew word is unclear.
Or “They will be ashamed.” The Hebrew can be read as a command or as a statement.

subheads.14: Neighbors Pulled Up and Brought Back

verses.text: Yahweh said to me, “Go to the market and buy a linen belt.{a} Wrap it around your waist, and keep it out of water.”
So I bought a belt, just as Yahweh said, and tied it around my waist.
Then Yahweh’s word came to me a second time.
He said, “Take the belt that you bought and are wearing. Travel to Perath{b} and tuck it in a gap between rocks there.”
So I went and hid it at Perath, as Yahweh ordered.
Many days passed. Then Yahweh said to me, “Travel again to Perath and take out the belt I told you to hide.”
So I went to Perath and dug the belt out of its hiding place. But the belt was rotten. It was good for nothing.
Then Yahweh’s word came to me again.
He said, “In the same way I will rot the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.
This wicked people will not hear My words. They follow their own stubborn hearts and run after other gods to serve and bow down to. They will turn out like this belt, useless.
As a belt clings to a person’s waist, I made all of Israel and all of Judah cling to Me,” announces Yahweh. “They were to be My people, My fame, My praise, and My pride. But they would not listen.”
“Tell them this message as well: ‘Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: Every wine jar will be filled with wine.’ They may reply, ‘Of course we know that wine jars get filled with wine!’
Then tell them, ‘Yahweh says: I am about to fill everyone in this land with drunkenness. That includes the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and everyone in Jerusalem.
I will knock them against each other, fathers and sons together,’ announces Yahweh. ‘I will not hold back or feel sorry. I will not show mercy, and I will destroy them.’”

Listen carefully. Do not act proud,
because Yahweh has spoken.

Give glory to Yahweh your God
before He sends the darkness,
before your feet stumble
on the shadowy hills.
You hope for light,

but if you will not listen,
I will cry alone in secret because of your pride.
My eyes will pour out bitter tears,
flowing and flowing,
because Yahweh’s flock has been taken prisoner.

Tell the king and the queen mother:{c}
“Step down and sit on the ground,
because your glorious crowns
have fallen from your heads.”

The towns in the Negev{d} are locked up,
and no one can open them.
All Judah is taken away,
every last person.

Lift your eyes and see
those marching from the north.
Where is the flock you were given,
your lovely flock?

What will you say when Yahweh puts rulers over you,
the very people you taught
to be your close friends?{e}
Will pain not grab you
like a woman in labor?

You may ask yourself,
“Why did this happen to me?”
Your huge guilt is the reason
your clothing was torn away
and you were treated roughly.{f}

Can a Cushite{g} change his skin color?
Can a leopard take off its spots?
Then you could also do good,
you who are trained in doing evil.

“I will scatter you like straw
blown by the desert wind.

This is your portion,
the share I have measured out for you,” announces Yahweh,
“because you forgot Me
and trusted in lies.

I Myself will lift your skirts over your face,
so everyone sees your shame.

I have seen your unfaithful acts:
your wild desires and cries,
your shameless prostitution
on the hills and in the fields.
Shame on you, Jerusalem!
How long will you stay unclean?”

notes.text: Hebrew ezor, a linen loincloth worn next to the skin. See 13:1.

Hebrew Perat. It is usually the Euphrates River, far to the northeast. Some think it was a nearby place called Parah, about 3 miles (5 km) from Anathoth. The Euphrates fits the later message about Babylon.
The queen mother was a powerful person in Judah’s court. Here she was probably Nehushta, mother of King Jehoiachin. See 2 Kings 24:8.
The Negev is the dry southern region of Judah.
The Hebrew of this verse is hard to read.
Hebrew “your heels were treated violently,” meaning your clothing was torn off and you were disgraced.
Cush was the land south of Egypt, in what is now Sudan.

subheads.15: Hear and Do Not Be Proud
subheads.20: A Skin and Spots That Cannot Change

verses.text: This message from Yahweh came to Jeremiah when the rains stopped and the land dried up.{a}

“Judah is in mourning.
Her town gates sag with grief.
Her people sit on the ground dressed in black.
A loud wail rises from Jerusalem.

Rich men send their servants out to get water.
The servants walk to the cisterns,
but every one is dry.
They trudge home with empty jars.
Embarrassed and ashamed,
they cover their heads.

The ground is split open
because no rain has come.
The farmers are upset,
and they hide their faces too.

Even a doe in the open country
leaves the fawn she just had,
since the grass is all gone.

On the bare heights the wild donkeys stand
panting like jackals.
Their eyes go dull,
for nothing green is growing.

“Yahweh, our own sins accuse us.
Even so, act for the sake of Your name.
Time after time we have strayed from You.
We have done wrong to You.

You are the One Israel hopes in.
You save us when hard times come.
So why do You act like a stranger here,
like a traveler who stays just one night and moves on?

Why are You like a man caught by surprise,
like a soldier who has no power to save?
Yahweh, You are right here with us.
We are called by Your name.
Please do not leave us!”

Yahweh says this about these people:
“They love to roam from one thing to another.
They never hold their feet still.
So Yahweh is not pleased with them.
Now He will remember the wrong they did
and make them pay for their sins.”
Then Yahweh told me, “Stop praying that things will go well for these people.

They may fast, but I will close My ears to their cries. They may offer Me burnt offerings and grain offerings, but I will refuse them. Instead, I will put an end to them with the sword, starvation, and sickness.”
I answered, “Oh, Lord Yahweh! The prophets keep telling the people, ‘War will never reach you, and you will not go hungry. God will give you real peace in this place, and it will last.’”

Yahweh said to me, “Those prophets are using My name to tell lies. I never sent them. I gave them no orders, and I never talked with them. What they tell you are fake visions, empty magic, and ideas their own minds{b} made up.

So this is My message, says Yahweh, about the prophets who claim to speak for Me though I never sent them. They keep promising that sword and famine will never touch this land. But sword and famine are exactly how those prophets will die.

And the people who listen to them will be tossed out into Jerusalem’s streets, killed by sword and famine. There will be no one to bury any of them, not the men, not their wives, not their children. I will pour out on them the punishment their evil has earned.

“Say this to the people:
‘Let tears run from my eyes
all night and all day without a break.
My dear people, like a young daughter,
have been badly hurt.
The wound is deep and painful.

If I walk out to the fields,
there lie the ones the sword has killed.
If I enter the town,
there lie the ones starving and sick.
Even the prophets and the priests
wander through a land they do not understand.’”{c}

Yahweh, have You thrown Judah away for good?
Do You hate Zion with all Your heart?
Why have You struck us so hard
that nothing can heal us?
We hoped for peace,
yet nothing good ever arrived.
We looked for healing,
and found only terror.

We confess our evil, Yahweh,
and the guilt of our ancestors.
It is true. We have sinned against You.

Do not reject us. Your name is at stake.
Do not let Your glorious throne be shamed.
Remember the agreement You made with us.
Please do not break it.

Do the worthless idols of other nations bring rain?
Do the skies pour down showers on their own?
No, Yahweh our God, it is You.
So we wait for You,
since You alone make all of this happen.

notes.text: Hebrew “the droughts” or “the times of dryness.”
Hebrew “heart.” In the Bible the heart is often the place where a person thinks and makes plans.
The meaning of the Hebrew in this last line is not certain. It may mean they “go off to trade in a land they do not know.”

verses.text: Then Yahweh said to me, “Moses and Samuel could come and plead with Me for these people, and still My heart would not go out to them. Send them away from Me. Let them go!

They may ask you, ‘Where can we go?’ Then give them this answer from Yahweh:
‘Some are meant to die of disease,
and they will die that way.
Some are meant to die in war,
and war will kill them.
Some are meant to die of hunger,
and they will starve.
Some are meant to be taken prisoner,
and they will be dragged away.’

“I will send four kinds of killers against them,” Yahweh announces. “Swords will kill them. Dogs will pull their bodies away. Then the birds in the air and the wild animals on the land will eat what is left.
Every kingdom in the world will be horrified at what happens to them. It is because of the evil done in Jerusalem by Manasseh,{a} Hezekiah’s son, who was king of Judah.

“Jerusalem, who will feel sorry for you?
Who will cry for you?
Who will even stop by
to ask if you are all right?

You have walked away from Me,” Yahweh announces.
“You keep turning your back on Me.
So I will reach out My hand and ruin you.
I am tired of holding back.

I will scatter them the way a farmer separates grain from straw
with a pitchfork at the town gates.
I will take away their children.
I will destroy My people,
because they will not stop doing evil.

I will make their widows more in number
than the sand along the sea.
In the middle of the day I will send a killer
to strike the mothers of young men.
Suddenly I will fill them
with terror and fear.

A mother who had seven sons will grow weak.
She will gasp for breath.
Her sun will go down while it is still day.
She will be shamed and disgraced.
And any of her people who are still alive,
I will hand over to be killed by the sword
in front of their enemies,” Yahweh announces.

My mother, I wish you had never given birth to me!
Everywhere in this land
people argue and fight with me.
I have never lent money to anyone,
and I have never borrowed money.
Even so, everyone curses me.

Yahweh said, “I will surely free you for a good purpose.{b}
I will surely make your enemies
beg you for help
when trouble and disaster come.

Your wealth and treasures I will give away as loot,
free of charge.
That is the price of all the sins
you have done in every corner of your land.

Your enemies will become your masters{d}
in a country strange to you.
My anger has been set ablaze like a fire,
and it will burn against you.”

Yahweh, You know what I am going through.
Remember me and take care of me.
Pay back those who chase after me.
You are patient with them,
but do not let that patience cost me my life.
Think of how I am insulted because I serve You.

Your words came to me, and I took them in like food.
They made me happy.
They filled my heart with joy.
Yahweh, God of Armies,
I belong to You, and I carry Your name.

I never sat with the party crowd.
I never laughed and celebrated with them.
Your hand was on me, so I kept to myself.
You had made me full of Your anger at their sin.

Why does my pain never stop?
Why will my wound not heal?
Will You be like a creek that dries up in summer,
water I cannot count on?

So Yahweh replied,
“Come back to Me,
and I will bring you back
to stand in My service.
Stop saying worthless things
and say what really matters.
Then you will speak for Me.
Let the people come over to your side,
but do not go over to theirs.

I will make you strong for these people,
like a city wall made of bronze.
They will fight against you,
but they will never win.
I am at your side
to rescue you and keep you safe,” Yahweh announces.

“I will pull you out of the grip of evil people.
I will free you from the hands of cruel men.”

notes.text: Manasseh ruled Judah about 697–642 B.C. The evil he did is told in 2 Kings 21:1–18. Manasseh means “making to forget.”
The Hebrew in verses 11 and 12 is hard to understand, and the Greek Old Testament (the Septuagint) reads quite differently.
Or “Can iron and bronze break the iron from the north?”
Many Hebrew copies and the Septuagint say “make you serve your enemies” (compare 17:4). Other Hebrew copies say “make your enemies pass through.”

subheads.5: Who Will Feel Sorry for Jerusalem?

verses.text: Then Yahweh spoke to me again. He said,
“You must not take a wife. You must not raise a family in this place.
I am telling you what will happen to the children born here, to their mothers, and to their fathers in this land.

They will die of terrible diseases. Not a single person will mourn them or give them a grave. Their corpses will be left lying in the open like manure. Sword and starvation will finish them off, and vultures and wild beasts will feed on what remains.”

Yahweh says, “Do not go into a house where people are holding a funeral meal.{a} Do not go there to weep or to comfort them. My peace has been taken from this people,” Yahweh announces. “I have taken away My faithful love and My kindness.{b}
The great and the small alike will die in this land, and they will lie unburied. Nobody will mourn. Nobody will gash his body or shave his head in grief for them.
Nobody will bring food to comfort those who are grieving over the dead. Nobody will give them a drink to comfort them, not even when a father or a mother dies.
“And stay away from any house where a feast is going on. Do not join them at the table for food and wine.

Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Pay attention! While you are still alive, you will see Me put an end to every happy sound in this place. There will be no more laughing and celebrating. There will be no more cheerful voices of a groom and his bride.
“You will tell these people all this. Then they will ask you, ‘Why has Yahweh threatened us with such a terrible disaster? What is our crime? What have we ever done to offend Yahweh our God?’
Then tell them this: ‘Yahweh says, “It is because your ancestors left Me. They chased after other gods. They worshiped and served them. They walked away from Me and did not obey My teaching.
And each of you has acted even worse than they did. You stubbornly follow your own evil hearts, and none of you listens to Me.
That is why I will hurl you out of this country into a land unknown to you and to your ancestors. There you will serve other gods day and night, because I will show you no kindness.”’
“But a day is coming,” Yahweh announces, “when people will stop making promises by saying, ‘As sure as Yahweh lives, the One who led the Israelites out of Egypt.’

Instead, they will say, ‘As sure as Yahweh lives, the One who led the Israelites out of the north country and out of every other land where He had scattered them.’ Yes, I will return them to their own soil, which I gave to their ancestors.

“But for now I am sending for many fishermen,” Yahweh announces. “They will catch these people like fish. After that I will send for many hunters. They will track them down on every mountain and every hill and in the cracks of the rocks.
I watch everything they do. Nothing they do is hidden from Me. Their sin cannot be kept out of My sight.

First{c} I will make them pay twice over for their wrong and their sin. They have made My land unclean with the lifeless shapes of their disgusting idols. They have filled the land that belongs to Me with their hateful gods.”

Yahweh, You give me strength and keep me safe like a fortress.
When trouble comes, I run to You.
Nations from the ends of the earth will come to You.
They will say, “Our ancestors owned nothing but lies,
false gods that were useless and empty.

Can people make their own gods?
Things like that are no gods!”

“So I will teach them,” Yahweh says.
“This time I will make them understand
how strong and mighty My hand is.
Then they will know that My name is Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew marzeach, a special meal held to mourn the dead.
The Septuagint does not have “My faithful love and My kindness” or the first half of verse 6.
The Septuagint does not have the word “First.”

subheads.19: The Nations Will Turn to Yahweh

verses.text: “Judah’s sin has been cut into stone with an iron tool. A point of hard diamond{a} scraped it into their hearts. It is carved on the horns of their altars too.{b}
Their children even think about those altars. They remember the Asherah poles{c} under every green tree and on the high hills.
My mountain in the open country, I will give away your wealth and all your treasures as loot. I will do the same to your hilltop shrines, because of the sin spread across your land.

The land I gave you will slip from your grasp, and you will have caused it. In a country you have never seen, you will be slaves to your enemies. My anger is a fire that you lit, and it will never go out.”
Yahweh says: “Anyone who trusts in human strength is under a curse. That person leans on weak flesh, and his heart turns away from Yahweh.
He will be like a desert bush{d} in the dry plain. Good times will pass him by and he will not notice. He will live on baked ground in the wasteland, in salty soil where nobody can live.
“But the person who trusts in Yahweh is happy. Yahweh Himself is the one he counts on.

He is like a tree growing next to a river, sending its roots toward the water. When heat comes, it is not afraid. Its leaves stay green. When no rain falls, it does not fret, and the fruit keeps coming.”
Nothing is as crooked{e} as the human heart. It is sick past healing. Who could ever know it?
“I, Yahweh, search every heart. I test the deepest thoughts. I give each person what his life has earned, the result of what he has done.”
A bird may sit on eggs it never laid. A man who gets rich by cheating is like that bird. His wealth leaves him in the middle of his life, and in the end he looks like a fool.
From the beginning, our holy place has been a glorious throne raised up high.
Yahweh, You are Israel’s hope. All who leave You will be ashamed. Those who turn away from You{f} will have their names written in the dust. They have left Yahweh, the fountain of fresh water.
Yahweh, make me whole, and I will be whole. Save me, and I will be saved. My praise belongs to You alone.
Listen to what people say to me. “Where is the message from Yahweh? Let it happen now!”
I never begged You to send a disaster.{g} I never wanted that terrible day to come. You know this. You heard every word that came from my mouth.
Do not frighten me. You are my safe place when trouble comes.
Make those who chase me feel shame, but not me. Let them be terrified, but not me. Bring the day of trouble on them. Break them again and again!
Yahweh said to me, “Take your place in the People’s Gate.{h} Kings of Judah walk through it when they leave the city and when they return. Go to every other gate of Jerusalem too.
Say this to them: ‘Kings of Judah, listen to Yahweh’s message. So must all of Judah and everyone in Jerusalem who comes through these gates.
Yahweh says: Watch yourselves! On the Sabbath day you must not haul any burden, and you must not carry one into Jerusalem through its gates.
Do not take a load out of your houses on the Sabbath. Do no work of any kind. Make the Sabbath day holy, just as I ordered your ancestors.
But they would not listen. They paid no attention. They were stubborn and refused to hear Me or learn from Me.
But if you truly obey Me,” Yahweh announces, “and you stop bringing burdens through this city’s gates on the Sabbath, and you set that day apart by not working,

then kings who sit on David’s throne will come through these gates, and so will their officials. They will ride in chariots or on horses. The men of Judah and the people living in Jerusalem will come with them. This city will have people in it for all time.

People will arrive from the towns of Judah, from the villages around Jerusalem, from Benjamin’s land, from the Shephelah,{i} from the hills, and from the Negev. They will carry burnt offerings and other sacrifices to Yahweh’s house. Some will bring grain gifts and incense. Others will bring thank offerings.

“But if you refuse to listen, and you will not keep the Sabbath day holy, and you carry loads through the gates of Jerusalem on that day, then I will start a fire at those gates. It will burn up the palaces of Jerusalem, and nobody will put it out.’”

notes.text: Hebrew shamir, a very hard stone, perhaps emery or diamond.
The Septuagint does not have verses 1-4. Verses 3-4 partly repeat 15:13-14.
Asherah was a Canaanite goddess. Her symbol was a wooden pole or a carved tree.
Hebrew ar’ar, a desert shrub, perhaps a juniper or a small tamarisk. The Septuagint has “wild tamarisk.”
Hebrew aqov, “crooked, tricky.” It sounds like the name Jacob.
Hebrew “from Me.”
Or, with a small change, “I never ran away from being a shepherd who follows You.” The Hebrew is hard to understand.
Or “the Gate of the Sons of the People.” Nobody knows where it stood.
Shephelah means “lowland.” It is the low hills between Judah’s hill country and the coastal plain.

subheads.5: Trust in People or in Yahweh

verses.text: Yahweh gave Jeremiah a message.
“Go at once to the house of a potter. I will give you My words when you get there.”
I went to the potter’s shop. He was sitting at his work, spinning a two-part wheel.{a}
A pot he was making from clay came out ruined in his hands. So he squeezed the clay into a lump and shaped a different pot, one that pleased him.
Then a message from Yahweh came to me.
“People of Israel, am I not free to do with you what this potter did?” Yahweh asks. “You are in My hands the way clay is in the potter’s hands.
Sometimes I announce that I will pull up a nation or a kingdom, tear it down, and wipe it out.
If that nation gives up its wicked ways after My warning, I change My mind. I do not send the disaster I had planned.
Other times I announce that I will build up a nation or a kingdom and plant it.
If that nation does evil in My eyes and will not obey Me, I change My mind about the good I promised it.

So now, speak to Judah’s men and to everyone in Jerusalem: ‘Yahweh says this. Right now I am forming a disaster against you, and I am drawing up plans to hit you. Each of you, leave your evil road. Fix how you live and what you do.’
But they will say, ‘Forget it! We will follow our own plans. Each one of us will do whatever his stubborn, wicked heart wants.’”

So Yahweh says this:
“Ask the nations around you.
Has any of them heard of this before?
Virgin Israel has done a horrible thing.

Do the snows of Lebanon ever melt from its rocky heights?{b}
Do the cold streams that flow from far away ever dry up?{c}

Yet My people have forgotten Me.
They burn incense to empty idols.
Those idols made them stumble on the old, ancient roads.
Now they walk on side paths,
not on a road that has been built up.
Their land will turn into a sight that makes travelers gasp. People will whistle at it for all time. Everyone walking by will stand stunned and shake their heads.
I will scatter them before their enemies as an east wind scatters dust. When their day of ruin arrives, they will see My back and not My face.”{d}

Some people said, “Come on, let’s make plans against Jeremiah. We will always have priests to teach us, wise men to advise us, and prophets to speak for God. Let’s tear him down with our words. Let’s not listen to any of his messages.”

Yahweh, pay attention to me!
Hear what my opponents say about me.

Is evil the right reward for kindness?
Yet they have dug a pit to catch me.
Remember, I stood in Your presence
and spoke up for them,
hoping Your fury would leave them alone.

So let their children go hungry.
Give them over to the power of the sword.
Let wives lose their sons and their husbands.
Let death strike down the men,
and let the sword cut down the young soldiers in battle.

Let screams ring out from their homes
when You suddenly send raiders against them.
They dug a pit to catch me.
They hid traps for my feet.

But You know, Yahweh,
every plan they have made to kill me.
Do not forgive their guilt.
Do not wipe their sin from Your sight.
Let them fall down in front of You.
Deal with them when You are angry.

notes.text: Hebrew “the two stones,” the upper and lower wheels of a potter’s wheel. His feet turned it.
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Perhaps “the rock of Sirion,” another name for Mount Hermon.
Or “Do foreign, cold, flowing waters ever get pulled up?” The Hebrew is hard.
The Hebrew letters can also be read with other vowels. Some ancient copies read “I will look at them.”

verses.text: Yahweh told me, “Go to a potter and buy a clay jar.{a} Ask a few elders of the people and a few of the senior priests to come with you.
