Walk to the Ben-Hinnom Valley, where the Potsherd Gate{b} opens onto it. Call out there the words I give you.

Say, ‘You kings of Judah, and all you who live in Jerusalem, hear what Yahweh of Armies, Israel’s God, declares. A disaster is coming to this place. It will be so awful that anyone who hears of it will feel his ears ring.

These people turned away from Me. They treated this place as if it belonged to strangers. They sent incense up to gods that they, their ancestors, and Judah’s kings had never even heard of. They stained this place with the blood of people who did no wrong.
They built places to worship Baal. There they burned their sons in fire as gifts to Baal. I never gave that order. I never even mentioned it. The idea never came into My thoughts.
So listen. The time is coming,” Yahweh announces, “when nobody will use the names Topheth or Ben-Hinnom Valley for this place any longer. It will be known as the Valley of Killing.

Right here I will empty out{c} the plans of Judah and Jerusalem, the way water is emptied from a jar. Their enemies will make them fall by the sword. Those hunting for their lives will find them. I will give their corpses to the birds of the sky and the animals of the land to eat.
I will turn this city into a shocking wreck. Everyone passing by will gasp and hiss when they see all its wounds.
Enemies will close in and press hard on the city. The people inside will be so hungry that they will turn to the bodies of their sons and daughters for food. Neighbors will even eat each other.’
“Then break the jar while the men who came with you are watching.
Tell them, ‘Yahweh of Armies says: I will break this people and this city, the way a person breaks a clay pot that can never be mended. The dead will be buried in Topheth until no more space is left.
This is how I will treat this place and everyone who lives in it,” Yahweh announces. “I will make this city just like Topheth.

Every house in Jerusalem will be unclean, and so will the royal palaces of Judah. They will be like Topheth. On those rooftops people made smoke for the stars of the sky and poured out wine for other gods.’”
Jeremiah went back from Topheth, where Yahweh had sent him to speak. He stood in the yard of Yahweh’s house and told all the people,
“Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Listen! I am about to bring on this city and on every town around it each disaster I promised. They have been stubborn and would not listen to My words.”

notes.text: Hebrew baqbuq, a flask with a narrow neck. The word sounds like the gurgle of pouring water.
Hebrew Harsith, perhaps the gate where broken pottery was thrown away.
Hebrew baqqothi, a word play on baqbuq, “jar” (verse 1).

verses.text: The priest Pashhur son of Immer was the officer in charge of Yahweh’s house. He heard Jeremiah announce these things.
So Pashhur had Jeremiah the prophet beaten. Then he fastened him into the stocks{a} at the Upper Gate of Benjamin, beside Yahweh’s house.
The next day Pashhur let him out. Jeremiah said to him, “Yahweh has given you a new name. It is no longer Pashhur. It is Magor-Missabib.{b}

Yahweh says: You will see terror yourself, and so will all your friends. Enemy swords will cut them down while you look on. I will hand all Judah over to the king of Babylon. He will march them off to Babylon and kill many with the sword.
I will give away everything valuable in this city. All its goods, its fine things, and every treasure of the kings of Judah will go to the enemy. They will grab it all and carry it to Babylon.
And you, Pashhur, will be taken prisoner with everyone in your house. You will go to Babylon. You will die there and be buried there, you and all the friends to whom you spoke lies in My name.”

Yahweh, You tricked me,{c} and I let myself be tricked.
You were stronger than I was, and You won.
Everybody laughs at me all day long.
They all make fun of me.

Every time I speak, I have to shout,
“Violence! Destruction!”
Yahweh’s message has brought me nothing
but insults and jokes, day after day.

I tell myself, “I will not think about Him.
I will never speak in His name again.”
But then it feels like a fire burning in my heart,
shut up inside my bones.
Holding it back wears me out,
and I just cannot.

I hear a lot of whispering.
“Terror on every side!
Report him! Yes, let’s report him!”
Even my close friends
are waiting for me to fall.
They say, “Maybe we can fool him.
Then we can win over him
and get even.”

But Yahweh stands beside me like a fierce, powerful fighter.
So those who chase me will trip and fail.
They will be badly shamed because they did not succeed.
Their disgrace will last forever and never be forgotten.

Yahweh of Armies, You test good people.
You see into their minds and hearts.
Let me watch You punish them,
because I have placed my case in Your hands.

Sing to Yahweh!
Give Yahweh praise!
He has saved the life of the poor
from the grip of wicked people.

Cursed be the day
I was born!
May the day my mother had me
never be called a blessing!

Cursed be the man who brought my father the news,
“A baby boy has been born to you!”
He made my father so happy.

May that man end up like the towns
Yahweh wiped out and did not pity.
May he hear screams at dawn
and battle cries at midday,

He did not let me die before birth.
My mother’s body could have been my grave,
and she would have stayed pregnant forever.

Why did I come out into the light at all?
All I see is trouble and sorrow.
My days will end in shame.

notes.text: Hebrew mahpeketh, perhaps a device that held a body bent in a twisted position.
Magor-Missabib means “terror all around.” The Septuagint has “Exile” in place of this name.
Or “You fooled me, and I was fooled.” The Hebrew verb pathah is used for luring someone, as in Exodus 22:16.

subheads.14: Jeremiah Wishes He Had Never Been Born

verses.text: Yahweh gave Jeremiah a message when King Zedekiah{a} sent two men to him: Pashhur, whose father was Malchiah, and the priest Zephaniah, whose father was Maaseiah. The two men said,
“Please ask Yahweh for us. Nebuchadrezzar{b} king of Babylon is attacking us. Maybe Yahweh will do one of His amazing acts for us, so that Nebuchadrezzar leaves.”
Jeremiah told them, “Give Zedekiah this answer:

‘The God of Israel, Yahweh, says: Your soldiers are fighting the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans{c} who have your city surrounded. I will turn the weapons in their hands around. I will pile them up in the middle of this city.
I Myself will fight against you. My arm will be strong and My hand held out. I will be furious, burning with great anger.
I will strike every living thing in this city, people and animals. They will die of a terrible sickness.

After that,” Yahweh announces, “I will give King Zedekiah of Judah to King Nebuchadrezzar of Babylon. So will his officials and the rest of the people who survive the sickness, the sword, and the hunger in this city. Their enemies, who are hunting for their lives, will get them. Nebuchadrezzar will kill them with swords. He will not hold back. He will have no pity or mercy.’
“Now give these people a message. Yahweh says: ‘Look, I am putting two roads in front of you. One leads to life. One leads to death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, by hunger, or by sickness. But whoever goes out and gives up to the Chaldeans who surround you will live. His life will be his only prize.{d}
I have turned against this city. I will bring it harm, not good,” Yahweh announces. “The king of Babylon will get it, and he will burn it down.’
“Tell the royal family of Judah: ‘Listen to Yahweh’s message.

Family of David, Yahweh says:
Judge fairly every morning.
Free the victim of robbery from the one who took advantage of him.
Otherwise My anger will burst out like a fire
that burns with nobody able to stop it,
since your deeds are so evil.

I am your enemy, city in the valley,
rocky town on the plain,” Yahweh announces.
“You boast, ‘Who would dare come down at us?
Who could ever get into our hideouts?’

You will get what your actions have earned,” Yahweh announces.
“I will set fire to the forest around the city.
It will burn up everything near it.’”

notes.text: Zedekiah means “Yahweh is right.” He was the last king of Judah (597-586 B.C.) and a son of Josiah.
Nebuchadrezzar is another spelling of Nebuchadnezzar. It is closer to the Babylonian name Nabu-kudurri-usur.
The Chaldeans (Hebrew Kasdim) were people from southern Babylonia. Their royal family ruled the Babylonian empire at this time.
That is, he will escape with nothing but his life.

subheads.8: Life or Death for the People

verses.text: Yahweh says: “Walk down to the house where Judah’s king lives. Say this there.
‘Hear Yahweh’s message, you who rule from David’s throne. Hear it, officials, and all your people who walk in by these gates.

Yahweh says: Do what is fair and right. Save the robbed person from his attacker. Never treat the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow badly, and never hurt them. Spill no innocent blood in this place.
If you really do these things, then kings who sit on David’s throne will keep coming through the gates of this palace. They will ride in chariots and on horses, with their officials and their people.
But if you will not obey, I make this promise by My own name,” Yahweh announces. “This palace will become a pile of ruins.’

About the palace where the kings of Judah live, Yahweh says:
“To Me you are as precious as Gilead,
as the top of Lebanon’s mountains.
But I will certainly make you a desert.
Your towns will have nobody living in them.

I will send in men to wreck you,
each one carrying his weapons.
They will cut down your best cedar beams
and toss them into the fire.
“People from many nations will walk past this city. They will ask each other, ‘Why would Yahweh treat so great a city like this?’
And the reply will be, ‘Because they broke the agreement{x} with Yahweh their God. They knelt to other gods and served those gods instead.’”

Do not cry for the dead king.{a}
Do not grieve for him.
Cry instead for the one who is leaving.
He will never come back
to see the land where he was born.
Yahweh says this about Shallum,{b} Josiah’s son. He became king of Judah after his father Josiah, and then he was taken from this place. “He will never come back here.
In the country where his captors took him, he will die. He will not see this land again.”

“How terrible for the man who builds his house by cheating,
and adds rooms upstairs by treating people unfairly!
He works his neighbor for free
and never gives him his pay.

He says, ‘I will build myself a huge house
with big rooms upstairs.’
So he cuts out wide windows,
covers the walls with cedar,
and paints it a bright red.

Do you prove you are a king by owning more cedar?{c}
Your father ate and drank well,
and he also did what was fair and right.
So things went well for him.

He defended people who were poor and needy.
So things went well.
Is that not what knowing Me means?”
Yahweh asks.

“But all you look at and care about
is making a dishonest profit,
killing innocent people,
and bullying and robbing others.”

So Yahweh says this about Jehoiakim,{d} Josiah’s son and king of Judah:
“Nobody will cry for him and say,
‘My brother, how sad!’ or ‘My sister, how sad!’
Nobody will cry for him and say,
‘Our master, how sad!’ or ‘Your Majesty, how sad!’

“Go up to Lebanon and cry out.
Raise your voice in Bashan.
Shout from the Abarim mountains,{f}
because all your allies have been crushed.

I talked to you while things were easy,
but you answered, ‘No, I will not listen.’
That has been your habit since you were young.
You have never once obeyed Me.

The wind will herd away all your leaders,
and your allies will be taken as prisoners.
You will then be ashamed and disgraced
for all your wickedness.

You live in Lebanon,
nested high among the cedars.
How you will moan{g} when the pains grab you,
pains like a woman in labor!”
“As surely as I live,” Yahweh announces, “Coniah{h} son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, could be the seal ring on My right hand, and I would still tear him off.
I will hand you over to the men who want your life, the ones you are afraid of. They are Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and the Chaldeans.
I will throw you and your mother out to a different country. You were not born there, but you will die there.
They will long to return to this land, but they will never come back.”

Is Coniah a broken, despised jar?
Is he a pot nobody wants?
Why were he and his children thrown out
into a country they did not know?

Land, land, land,
listen to Yahweh’s message!

Yahweh says:
“Write this man down as having no children.
He will not do well in his lifetime.
None of his children will do well,
or sit on David’s throne,
or rule over Judah again.”{i}

notes.text: That is, King Josiah, who was killed at Megiddo in 609 B.C. (2 Kings 23:29).
Shallum means “payback.” It is the personal name of King Jehoahaz, Josiah’s son, who ruled for three months.
Or “because you try to beat others at using cedar.”
Jehoiakim means “Yahweh raises up.” He ruled 609-598 B.C. (2 Kings 23:34-24:6).
2 Kings 24:6 says only that Jehoiakim “rested with his ancestors.” This message may have come true in a way that book does not describe.
The Abarim are the mountains east of the Dead Sea. Mount Nebo is one of them.
So the Septuagint and other ancient copies. The Hebrew can mean “how you will be pitied.”
Coniah is a short form of Jeconiah, also called Jehoiachin, which means “Yahweh makes firm.” He ruled three months.
Jehoiachin had sons (1 Chronicles 3:17-18), but none of them became king.
Hebrew berit, often translated “covenant.”

subheads.1: A Message for the King’s House

verses.text: “How terrible for the shepherds who destroy My flock and scatter the sheep in My pasture!” Yahweh announces.

So Yahweh, the God of Israel, says this to the shepherds who care for My people: “You scattered My sheep. You chased them off. You never looked after them. Now I will look at you, and I will pay you back for your evil deeds,” Yahweh announces.
“I Myself will gather My sheep who are still alive. I will bring them from every country where I sent them. I will lead them back to their own pasture. There they will have lambs and grow in number.
I will put new shepherds over them who will care for them. The sheep will not be afraid or terrified again. Not one will go missing,” Yahweh announces.

“Listen, days are coming,” Yahweh announces.
“From David’s family I will make a good Branch{a} grow.
A king will rule who uses good sense.
Fairness and justice will mark everything he does in the land.

While he reigns, Judah will be saved.
Israel will rest in safety.
People will call him by this name:
‘Yahweh Is Our Righteousness.’{b}
“So listen, days are coming,” Yahweh announces. “People will stop making this vow: ‘By the living Yahweh, who led Israel’s people up from Egypt.’

They will vow this instead: ‘By the living Yahweh, who led the descendants of Israel’s family home from the northern country and from every place I had driven them.’ Then they will settle again on their own soil.”{c}

About the prophets:
My heart is crushed inside me.
All my bones shake.
I am like a man who is drunk,
like someone overcome by wine,
because of Yahweh
and His holy words.

The land is full of people who cheat on their husbands and wives.
Because of the curse,{d} the whole country mourns.
The desert pastures are dry.
They walk a wicked path.
They use their strength for wrong.

“Prophets and priests alike have turned from God.
I have found their evil even in My own house,” Yahweh announces.

“So their path will turn
into slick ground in the dark.
They will be shoved and go down.
I will send disaster to them
during the year of their punishment,” Yahweh announces.

“I saw an ugly thing
in the prophets of Samaria.
They prophesied by Baal
and made My people Israel wander.

In the prophets of Jerusalem
I have noticed something worse.
They are unfaithful and live by lies.
They make evildoers stronger,
so no one quits his wickedness.
They are all like Sodom to Me,
and Jerusalem’s people are like Gomorrah.”

So Yahweh of Armies says this about the prophets:
“I will feed them bitter wormwood.
Their drink will be water mixed with poison.
Godlessness has gone out from Jerusalem’s prophets
to spread over the whole country.”

Yahweh of Armies says:
“Do not listen to what these prophets say to you.
They are filling you with empty hopes.{e}
They tell visions made up in their own minds.
Those visions did not come from Yahweh’s mouth.

They keep telling people who hate Me,
‘Yahweh says you will have peace.’
And they tell everyone who follows his own stubborn heart,
‘No disaster will touch you.’”

Look, a storm from Yahweh!
His rage has burst out.
A twisting wind
will come down hard on the wicked.

Yahweh’s anger will not turn back
until He has done
everything He set His mind to do.
Later on,
you will see this plainly.

“I never sent these prophets,
yet they raced off.
I never spoke to them,
yet they delivered messages.

If they had stood in My council,
they would have announced My words to My people.
Then My people would have left their evil road
and given up their wicked actions.

“Am I a God who stays close and nowhere else,” Yahweh asks,
“not a God who is far away too?

Can anyone hide in a secret place
where I cannot see him?” Yahweh asks.
“Do I not fill the sky and the earth?” Yahweh asks.
“I have heard the prophets who lie while using My name. They claim, ‘I dreamed it! I dreamed it!’
How long will this go on? Do these lying prophets have anything in their hearts but the tricks of their own minds?
These prophets plan to have My people forget My name through the dreams they swap. Long ago their ancestors lost My name too, when Baal took its place.
A prophet who has a dream should tell it as a dream. A prophet who has My word should give it faithfully. Straw and grain have nothing in common,” Yahweh announces.
“Is My word not like fire,” Yahweh asks, “and like a hammer that smashes rock?
“So I am against the prophets,” Yahweh announces, “who steal My words from one another.
I am against the prophets,” Yahweh announces, “who wag their tongues and say, ‘Yahweh declares!’

I am against those who prophesy false dreams,” Yahweh announces. “They pass them around and mislead My people with lies and big talk. I never sent them or put them in charge. They give these people no help at all,” Yahweh announces.
“If a citizen, a prophet, or a priest asks you, ‘What is Yahweh’s load?’{g} answer, ‘You are the load! And I will drop you,’ Yahweh announces.
If a prophet, a priest, or anyone else says ‘Yahweh’s load,’ I will punish that man and his family.
Each of you should ask your neighbor or relative, ‘What was Yahweh’s answer?’ or ‘What has Yahweh said?’
But never say ‘Yahweh’s load’ again. A person’s own words become his load, and you twist the words of the living God, Yahweh of Armies, our God.
This is what you should ask a prophet: ‘What did Yahweh answer you?’ or ‘What has Yahweh said?’
But suppose you keep saying ‘Yahweh’s load.’ Then Yahweh says: ‘I told you not to say “Yahweh’s load.” You said it anyway.
So I will lift you up{h} and hurl you from My sight. The same goes for the city I gave to you and your ancestors.
Shame will fall on you and stay forever. People will never forget your disgrace.’”

notes.text: Hebrew tsemach, “sprout” or “shoot.” It is a title for the future king from David’s family (33:15; Zechariah 3:8).
Hebrew Yahweh tsidqenu. It may be a play on the name of King Zedekiah, Tsidqiyyahu, “Yahweh is my right.”
The Septuagint puts verses 7-8 after verse 40. Verses 7-8 nearly repeat 16:14-15.
Or, with some ancient copies, “because of these things.”
Hebrew hevel, “breath” or “vapor.” They fill you with hopes that are empty.
Hebrew sod, the council of heavenly beings around Yahweh (compare 1 Kings 22:19-22).
Hebrew massa means both “load” and “message.” It is something “lifted up.”
Some Hebrew copies and ancient versions read “I will forget you completely,” which sounds almost the same in Hebrew.

subheads.1: Bad Shepherds and the Good King

verses.text: Yahweh showed me two baskets of figs placed in front of Yahweh’s temple. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had already carried Jeconiah{a} son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, off from Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar had also seized Judah’s officials, skilled workers, and metalworkers,{b} and taken them all to Babylon.
One basket held excellent figs, like the first to ripen. The other held terrible figs, so rotten that nobody could eat them.
Yahweh asked me, “Jeremiah, what do you see?” I said, “Figs. The good ones are very good. The bad ones are very bad, too rotten to eat.”
Next, Yahweh sent me this message.
“Yahweh, the God of Israel, says this: The good figs stand for the people of Judah I sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans. I will treat them as good.
I will keep watch over them for their good and lead them back to this land. I will build them up and never tear them down. I will plant them and never uproot them.
I will give them a heart that knows Me, so they will realize I am Yahweh. They will be My people, and I will be their God. Then they will turn back to Me with all their hearts.

“But I will treat King Zedekiah of Judah like the rotten figs that nobody can eat,” Yahweh says. “His officials will be treated the same. So will the survivors left behind in Jerusalem, and the ones who settled in Egypt.
I will make them a horror and a disaster{c} for every kingdom on earth. Wherever I scatter them, people will insult them, joke about them, mock them, and curse them.
I will send the sword, hunger, and sickness on them until they are gone from the land I gave them and their ancestors.”

notes.text: Jeconiah is another form of the name Jehoiachin (see the note at 22:24). He was taken away in 597 B.C.
Or “the smiths.” The Hebrew word masger may mean “locksmith” or “wall builder.”
Hebrew “a horror for disaster.” The Septuagint reads, “I will scatter them to every kingdom of the earth.”

verses.text: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah ruled Judah, Jeremiah received a word about all the people of Judah. That same year was Nebuchadrezzar’s first as king of Babylon.{a}
Jeremiah the prophet gave this word to everybody in Judah and everybody living in Jerusalem.

“Yahweh’s messages have been coming to me for twenty-three years now. They began in the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, and they have not stopped. I rose early again and again to tell you. You refused to listen.
Yahweh also kept sending you His servants the prophets, over and over. You never listened to them. You never even turned your ears their way.
Their message was this: ‘Each of you, quit your evil life and your wicked deeds. Then you can stay in the land Yahweh gave you and your ancestors, to keep from now on.
Do not chase after other gods to serve and kneel to them. Do not anger Me with figures your hands have made. If you obey, I will do you no harm.’
But you ignored Me,” Yahweh announces. “You made Me angry with your idols, and you brought harm on yourselves.{b}
“So Yahweh of Armies says: You would not obey My words.

Watch Me. I am calling every northern tribe,” Yahweh announces. “I am also calling My servant Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.{c} I will lead them to attack this land and everyone in it, and also the nations around it. I will set them apart for destruction.{d} They will become something people stare at in shock, whistle about, and call a ruin forever.
I will take away the sounds of laughing and singing. I will end the voices of the groom and the bride. There will be no hum of the grinding stone and no light from a lamp.
This whole country will turn into a ruined, horrible place. Babylon’s king will be served by these nations for seventy years.{e}
After those seventy years end, I will punish the king of Babylon and his nation for their guilt,” Yahweh announces. “I will turn the land of the Chaldeans into a wasteland for all time.
I will do to that land everything I have spoken against it. Every word written in this book will happen, the book where Jeremiah told about all the nations.{f}
Many nations and mighty kings will make slaves of the Babylonians too. I will pay them back for what they did and for everything their hands made.”{g}
Yahweh, the God of Israel, gave me this order: “Get this cup out of My hand. It holds the wine of My fury. Every nation I send you to must drink from it.
When they drink, they will wobble and act insane. A sword is coming among them, and I am the One who sends it.”
I took the cup out of Yahweh’s hand. Then I made every nation drink, one after another, wherever Yahweh sent me.
First came Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, with their kings and officials. They would become a ruin, a horror, something to hiss at, and a curse, as they are today.
Next came Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his leaders, and all his people,
and all the foreign peoples living there.{h} Then came all the kings of the land of Uz.{i} Then came all the Philistine kings, from Ashkelon, Gaza, and Ekron, and the few left in Ashdod.
Then came Edom, Moab, and the Ammonites.
Then came all the kings of Tyre and of Sidon, and the kings of the coastlands across the sea.
Then came Dedan, Tema, Buz, and everyone who cuts his hair at the temples.
Then came all the kings of Arabia, and all the kings of the foreign peoples camping in the desert.
Then came all the kings of Zimri,{j} Elam, and Media,
and every king of the north, near or far, in turn. Every kingdom on earth drank, in fact. After them all, the king of Sheshach{k} would drink.
“Then tell them, ‘Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Drink until you are drunk. Be sick. Fall and never rise again. I am sending a sword among you.’
And suppose they refuse to take the cup from you. Then tell them, ‘Yahweh of Armies says: You will drink it, like it or not!

Think about this. I have begun to bring disaster on the city that carries My name. Did you expect to escape? You will not escape. I am calling for a sword against everyone living on earth,’ Yahweh of Armies announces.

“Now speak all these words to them as a prophet. Tell them:
‘Yahweh roars from heaven.
From His holy home His voice thunders.
He roars loudly at His own land.
He shouts like people stomping on grapes.
His shout is aimed at everyone on earth.

The noise echoes to the ends of the earth,
because Yahweh has a charge to bring against the nations.
He is putting all people on trial.
He gives the wicked over to the sword,’
Yahweh announces.”

Yahweh of Armies says:
“Look, disaster is spreading
from one nation to the next.
A huge storm is rising
from the far corners of the earth.”
Those Yahweh kills on that day will be found everywhere, from one end of the earth to the other. Nobody will cry over them, collect them, or bury them. They will be like manure spread on the ground.

“Howl, you shepherds! Scream!
Roll in the dirt, you leaders of the flock.
Your time to be slaughtered has come.
You will be scattered{l}
and fall like a fine clay jar that breaks.

The shepherds will have nowhere to run.
The leaders of the flock will not escape.

Hear the shepherds screaming!
Hear the wailing of the flock’s leaders!
Yahweh is wrecking their pasture.

The calm sheep pens are destroyed
by Yahweh’s burning anger.

He has come out of His hiding place like a lion.
Their land is now a desert,
because of the cruel sword{m}
and Yahweh’s blazing anger.”

notes.text: That is, 605 B.C., the year of the battle of Carchemish (46:2). The Septuagint does not have the words in parentheses in the Hebrew text.
The Septuagint has most of verse 7 only as “But you did not listen to Me.”
The Septuagint does not have “and Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, My servant.”
Hebrew herem, total destruction set apart for God in holy war.
People count the seventy years in different ways: from 605 B.C. to the fall of Babylon in 539 B.C., or from the first Temple’s fall (586 B.C.) to its rebuilding.
In the Septuagint, verse 13 ends at “written in this book,” and the next words begin the messages about the nations.
The Septuagint does not have verse 14.
Or “all the mixed peoples.” Hebrew erev, perhaps foreign soldiers or settlers.
The Septuagint does not have “all the kings of the land of Uz.” Uz was a region east or southeast of Israel.
Zimri is not known from other places. It may be a code name like Sheshach (verse 26), or a copying mistake.
Sheshach is a code word for Babel (Babylon). It uses atbash, a scribe’s trick that swaps each Hebrew letter for its mirror letter in the alphabet.
The Hebrew is uncertain. Some read “and I will shatter you.”
So some Hebrew copies (compare 46:16; 50:16). The Septuagint has “the great sword.”

verses.text: Jehoiakim son of Josiah had just become king of Judah.{a} At that time Yahweh gave Jeremiah this message.
“Yahweh says: Stand in the yard of Yahweh’s house. Speak to the people from all the towns of Judah who come to worship there. Give them every word I tell you. Do not leave out a single one.
Maybe they will listen, and each person will turn from his evil life. Then I would change My mind about the disaster I plan to send because of their wicked deeds.
Tell them, ‘Yahweh says: You may refuse to listen to Me and to live by My teaching, which I put before you.
You may also ignore the prophets who serve Me. I keep sending them to you, early and often, and you have not listened.
If that is your choice, then this house will end up like Shiloh. This city will become a name that nations on earth use in their curses.’”
The priests, the prophets, and all the people listened as Jeremiah said this in Yahweh’s house.
Jeremiah finished telling the people everything Yahweh had ordered him to say. Right then the priests, the prophets, and all the people grabbed him. They shouted, “You must die!

How dare you announce in Yahweh’s name that this house will end up like Shiloh? How dare you say this city will be wrecked, with nobody living in it?” The whole crowd pushed in around Jeremiah in Yahweh’s house.
The officials of Judah heard about all this. They left the palace and went up to Yahweh’s house. They sat down at the entrance of the New Gate of Yahweh’s house.
The priests and prophets said to the officials and the crowd, “This man should be put to death. You heard it yourselves. He spoke against this city.”
Then Jeremiah spoke to all the officials and to everyone there. “Yahweh is the One who sent me. He told me to speak against this house and this city, and you have heard His very words.
So now, improve your lives and your actions. Obey Yahweh your God. Then Yahweh will give up the disaster He announced against you.
As for me, you have power over me. Treat me however you think is fair and right.

Only be sure of this: if you kill me, you will be guilty of shedding innocent blood. That guilt will stay on you, on this city, and on all who live in it. Yahweh truly did send me to tell you all these words, and you have heard them with your own ears.”
Then the officials and the crowd gave their answer to the priests and prophets. “No death sentence for this man! He speaks to us for Yahweh our God.”
Some of the elders of the land also stood up. They said to the whole crowd,

“Micah of Moresheth{b} was a prophet while Hezekiah ruled Judah. To everyone in Judah he said, ‘Yahweh of Armies says: Zion will be plowed under like a farm field. Jerusalem will turn into piles of rubble. Bushes and trees will grow wild over the mountain with the temple on it.’

Did King Hezekiah and all Judah kill Micah? No! Hezekiah honored Yahweh and begged Him for mercy. Then Yahweh changed His mind about the disaster He had announced. If we kill Jeremiah, we will pile a huge disaster on our own heads!”
Another man gave messages in Yahweh’s name too. His name was Uriah, and his father was Shemaiah. He came from Kiriath-Jearim. His words against this city and this land were very much like Jeremiah’s.
King Jehoiakim, all his soldiers, and all his officials heard what Uriah said. The king tried to have him killed. Uriah found out and was afraid. He ran away to Egypt.
King Jehoiakim sent men after him to Egypt. They were Elnathan son of Achbor{c} and some others.
They dragged Uriah back from Egypt and delivered him to King Jehoiakim. The king struck him down with a sword. Then he had the body tossed into the graveyard where ordinary people were buried.
But Ahikam son of Shaphan{d} supported Jeremiah. Because of him, Jeremiah was not given to the mob to be killed.

notes.text: That is, about 609 B.C. This chapter tells what happened at the temple sermon, which is also in chapter 7.
Micah of Moresheth is the prophet whose book is one of the Twelve. This quotation is Micah 3:12.
Elnathan means “God has given.” He may have been the father of Nehushta, King Jehoiachin’s mother (2 Kings 24:8).
Ahikam son of Shaphan served under King Josiah (2 Kings 22:12). He was the father of Gedaliah, who later became governor.

verses.text: Zedekiah{a} son of Josiah had just become king of Judah. Then Yahweh sent Jeremiah this message.
Yahweh said to me, “Make a wooden yoke and tie it on with leather straps. Wear it on your neck.
Then pass the word{b} to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon, using the envoys who have arrived in Jerusalem to visit Zedekiah, king of Judah.
Order them to tell their masters this: ‘Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says to tell your masters:
By My great power and My strong arm I created the earth, along with the people and animals living on it. Whoever I choose receives it.
I have now placed all these lands in the hands of My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. Even the wild animals are his to command.
Every nation will serve him, then his son, then his grandson. Then the time will come for his own land to fall. After that, many nations and powerful kings will make him their slave.{c}

Suppose a nation or kingdom refuses Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon as its master and will not bend under his yoke. I will punish that nation,” Yahweh announces. “I will use the sword, hunger, and sickness, until Nebuchadnezzar has wiped it out.
So ignore your prophets, your fortune-tellers, your dream readers,{d} and your magicians. They keep promising you, ‘The king of Babylon will never rule you.’
What they tell you is a lie. It will only take you far from your own country. I will push you out, and you will perish.
But a nation that bends its neck beneath Babylon’s yoke and serves that king will stay in its own land,” Yahweh announces. “Its people will farm the ground and live there.’”
To King Zedekiah of Judah I gave the very same warning. “Bow your necks beneath the yoke of Babylon’s king. Be loyal to him and his people, and stay alive.
Why die by the sword, by hunger, and by sickness, you and your people? Yahweh has warned that this is the fate of any nation that will not serve Babylon’s king.{e}
Do not pay attention to the prophets who say, ‘You will never have to serve the king of Babylon.’ They are speaking lies to you.
I did not send them,” Yahweh announces. “They are lying in My name. So I will drive you out, and you will die, both you and the prophets who speak to you.”

Then I turned to the priests and to everyone else. “Yahweh says: Do not listen to your prophets when they promise, ‘Soon the things from Yahweh’s house will come back from Babylon.’ They are telling you lies.
Do not listen to them. Work for the king of Babylon, and stay alive. Does this city have to become a ruin?{f}

If they really are prophets, and if they really have Yahweh’s word, let them beg Yahweh of Armies to keep the items still in Yahweh’s house, in the king’s palace, and in Jerusalem from going to Babylon.
Yahweh of Armies has spoken about the pillars,{g} the huge bronze basin, the stands on wheels, and whatever else remains in this city.
When Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, off to Babylon, he left these things behind. He did take the other nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.
Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says this about the things left in Yahweh’s house, in the king’s palace, and in Jerusalem:{h}
‘They will be carried to Babylon. There they will sit until I come for them,’ Yahweh announces. ‘Then I will bring them back up and put them again in this place.’”

notes.text: So a few Hebrew copies and the Syriac (compare verses 3 and 12, and 28:1). The usual Hebrew text says Jehoiakim.
Hebrew “send them.” Jeremiah’s yoke, used as a sign, is told about in 28:10-11.
The Septuagint does not have verse 7.
Hebrew “your dreams.”
The Septuagint does not have verse 13. Its text of verses 12-22 is much shorter throughout.
The Septuagint does not have verse 17.
The two bronze pillars Jachin and Boaz, the huge bronze basin called “the sea,” and the stands on wheels.
The Septuagint does not have verse 21 or the last sentence of verse 22. It ends, “they will go into Babylon.”

subheads.16: Do Not Trust the Lying Prophets

verses.text: In the fifth month (in July–August){b} of that same year, Zedekiah’s fourth year{a} as king of Judah, something happened in Yahweh’s house. Hananiah{c} son of Azzur, a prophet from Gibeon, confronted me while priests and crowds looked on.
He said, “This is the message of Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: Babylon’s king no longer has his yoke on you. I have broken it.
Two years from now, everything that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon carried away from Yahweh’s house to Babylon will be back in this place.
Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, will come home as well, along with all the Judeans who went to Babylon as captives,” Yahweh announces. “Yes, I will smash the yoke of the king of Babylon.”
Then Jeremiah the prophet replied to Hananiah the prophet. The priests and everyone standing in Yahweh’s house heard it.
Jeremiah said, “Amen! I hope Yahweh does exactly that. I hope Yahweh makes your message come true, and brings the things from Yahweh’s house and all the prisoners home from Babylon.
But now listen to what I must say to you and to all these people.
Prophets who lived long before you and me gave warnings. They spoke of war, disaster, and sickness for many countries and great kingdoms.
But when a prophet promises peace, nobody will know whether Yahweh really sent him until his words come true.”
Hananiah the prophet then lifted the yoke off Jeremiah’s neck and snapped it in two.

Hananiah told all the people, “Yahweh says: In the same way, within two years I will snap the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon off the neck of every nation.” After that, Jeremiah the prophet walked away.
Some time after Hananiah broke the yoke off Jeremiah’s neck, Yahweh gave Jeremiah a message.
“Go to Hananiah and tell him, ‘Yahweh says: You broke a wooden yoke. But you will make{d} an iron one to take its place.
Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: I have fastened an iron yoke around all these nations. They must serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will. Even the wild animals are his.’”
Then Jeremiah told Hananiah, “Hear me, Hananiah! Yahweh did not send you. You have made these people trust a lie.
So Yahweh says: I am about to remove you{e} from the face of the earth. You will die this year, because you taught rebellion against Yahweh.”
In the seventh month (in September–October) of that very year, the prophet Hananiah died.{f}

notes.text: That is, 594-593 B.C. The Septuagint says only “in the fourth year of Zedekiah king of Judah.”
Hebrew “the fifth month,” Av.
Hananiah means “Yahweh has been kind.” The Septuagint calls him “the false prophet.”
So the Hebrew. The Septuagint reads “I will make.”
Hebrew meshallechakha, a play on the word “send” (shalach) in verse 15. Yahweh did not send Hananiah, so Yahweh would send him away.
Hebrew “the seventh month,” Tishri, about two months after the meeting in verse 1. The Septuagint does not have this verse’s date.

verses.text: Jeremiah the prophet wrote a letter in Jerusalem. He sent it to the elders who were still alive among the exiles, to the priests and prophets, and to all the people Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem to Babylon.

This happened after King Jeconiah had left Jerusalem. He took the queen mother and palace officials{a} with him. Judah’s and Jerusalem’s leaders went along, as did the skilled workers and the metalworkers.
Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah carried the letter. King Zedekiah of Judah was sending them to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The letter said:
“Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, speaks to every exile I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Put up houses and live in them. Start gardens and eat what grows in them.
Marry, and raise sons and daughters. Let your sons take wives and your daughters take husbands, so that they raise children too. Increase in number there. Do not become fewer.
Care about the well-being{b} of the city I sent you to. Pray to Yahweh for it, because your own well-being depends on its well-being.
Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, also says: Do not let the prophets and fortune-tellers among you fool you. Do not trust the dreams you encourage them to have.{c}
They are speaking lies to you in My name. I did not send them,” Yahweh announces.
Yahweh says: “When Babylon has had seventy years, I will visit you. I will do what I kindly promised, and I will lead you home to this place.
I am the One who knows My plans for you,” Yahweh announces. “They are plans for peace and not for harm. They will give you a hopeful future.{d}
Then you will call out to Me. You will pray, and I will hear every word.
You will look for Me and find Me, if you search with your whole heart.

I will let you find Me,” Yahweh announces. “I will undo your captivity. I will collect you from every nation and place where I scattered you. I will take you home to the very place I removed you from.{e}
You have said, ‘Yahweh has given us prophets here in Babylon.’
Hear what Yahweh says about the king on David’s throne and about everyone still living in this city, your relatives who were not taken with you:{f}
Yahweh of Armies says: I am sending sword, hunger, and sickness among them. I will treat them like figs gone bad, too rotten to eat.
I will chase them with sword, hunger, and sickness. Every kingdom on earth will be horrified by them. They will be cursed, ruined, hissed at, and insulted in every nation where I have scattered them.
They would not listen to the words I kept sending through My servants the prophets, early and often,” Yahweh announces. “And you would not listen either.”
Now hear Yahweh’s message, all you exiles I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

Now hear what Yahweh of Armies says, the God of Israel, about two men: Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah. They are lying to you while using My name. I am giving them to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will execute them while you watch.
They will become part of a curse among all the exiles of Judah in Babylon: ‘May Yahweh make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon burned in a fire.’{g}
They did shameful things in Israel. They slept with their neighbors’ wives. They also spoke lies in My name that I never told them to say. I know it all, and I saw it myself,” Yahweh announces.
Tell Shemaiah the Nehelamite:{h}

This is the word of Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: You wrote letters under your own name and sent them to everybody in Jerusalem. You sent one to the priest Zephaniah, who is Maaseiah’s son, and one to every other priest. You said,
‘Yahweh has put you in Jehoiada’s place as priest. You have charge of Yahweh’s house. Any madman who acts like a prophet should be locked in the stocks and an iron collar.
So why have you not stopped Jeremiah of Anathoth, who is speaking as a prophet to you?
He even sent word to us in Babylon. He wrote, “The exile will be long. Put up houses and live in them. Start gardens and eat what grows in them.”’”
The priest Zephaniah read this letter out loud while Jeremiah the prophet listened.
Then Yahweh gave Jeremiah a message.
“Send this to all the exiles: ‘Yahweh says this about Shemaiah the Nehelamite. Shemaiah spoke to you as a prophet, but I never sent him. He made you trust a lie.

So Yahweh says: I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his family line. None of his people will be alive among these people to see what good I will do for My people,” Yahweh announces. “He preached rebellion against Yahweh.’”

notes.text: Hebrew sarisim, often “eunuchs,” but also a general word for court officials.
Hebrew shalom, “peace,” “good,” or “wholeness.” It is used three times in this verse.
Hebrew “your dreams that you cause to be dreamed.” The Septuagint reads “your dreams, which you dream.”
Hebrew “an end (acharit) and a hope,” that is, a hopeful future.
The Septuagint has only “And I will appear to you” for most of verse 14.
The Septuagint does not have verses 16-20.
Hebrew qalam, “roasted.” It is a play on qelalah, “curse,” and on the name Kolaiah (verse 21).
Nehelamite may mean “from Nehelam,” a place nobody knows. It may also hint at the Hebrew word chalam, “to dream.”

verses.text: Yahweh gave Jeremiah another message.
“Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: Write all My words that I have spoken to you in a book.{a}

The days are coming,” Yahweh announces, “when I will turn things around for My people, Israel and Judah. The land I gave their ancestors will be theirs again. I will return them to it, and they will possess it.”
Yahweh spoke these words about Israel and Judah.

Yahweh says:
“We hear cries of terror,
fear, with no peace anywhere.

Ask and think about this:
can a man give birth?
Then why do I see every man
holding his stomach like a woman in labor?
Why are all the faces white with fear?

How awful! No day has ever been like that one.
It will be a time of misery for Jacob,
yet Jacob will come through it safely.

“On that day,” Yahweh of Armies announces,
“I will break the yoke off your{b} neck.
I will rip off the straps that tie it on.
Foreigners will not make him their slave again.

They will serve Yahweh their God instead,
and David, the king
I will raise up for them.

“As for you, Jacob, My servant, do not be afraid,” Yahweh announces.
“Israel, do not be shaken.
Look, I will rescue you from far away.
I will rescue your children from the country where they are prisoners.
Jacob will return, and he will be calm and safe.
Nobody will scare him.

I am with you,” Yahweh announces. “I will rescue you.
Every nation where I scattered you
I will finish off completely.
But you I will not finish off.
I will correct you, but fairly.
I will never let you go without any punishment.”{c}

Yahweh says:
“Your injury cannot be fixed.
Your wound will not heal.

All your lovers have forgotten you.
You do not matter to them now.
I hit you the way an enemy would,
with the harsh punishment of a cruel man,
because your guilt is so big
and your sins are so many.

Why do you scream about your injury?
Your pain has no cure.
Your guilt is so big and your sins are so many
that I did these things to you.{e}

But all who swallow you up will be swallowed up.
All your enemies will go off as prisoners.
Those who rob you will be robbed.
Those who loot you I will hand over to be looted.

I will grow new skin over you
and heal your wounds,” Yahweh announces.
“People call you an outcast.
They say, ‘That is Zion. Nobody cares about her.’

“Yahweh says this:
Look, I will reverse the fortunes of Jacob’s tents.
I will have pity on his homes.
On its old ruins the city will go up again.{f}
The palace will stand where it belongs.

Songs of thanks will come from the people.
So will the sound of happy laughter.
I will make them grow, and they will not become few.
I will give them honor, and they will not be thought small.

Their children will be like those of long ago.
Their community will stand firm in My presence.
I will punish everyone who is cruel to them.

A ruler will rise from their own number.
A leader will step out from among them.
I will call him near, and he will come to Me.
Who else would dare
to come near Me?” Yahweh asks.

“You will be My people,
and I will be your God.”{g}

Look at Yahweh’s storm!
His fury has gone out.
A whirlwind will swirl
over the heads of wicked people.

Yahweh’s blazing anger will not turn away
until He has done what He planned.
He will complete
what His heart intended.
In the last days
you will understand.{h}

notes.text: Hebrew sefer, a scroll or book. Chapters 30-31 are often called “the Book of Comfort.”
So the Hebrew. The Septuagint reads “their neck.”
The Septuagint does not have verses 10-11. They appear again at 46:27-28.
The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
The Septuagint does not have verse 15.
Hebrew tel, a mound of ruins built up from earlier towns on the same spot.
The Septuagint does not have verse 22.
Verses 23-24 nearly repeat 23:19-20.

subheads.1: A Promise to Bring Them Home
subheads.12: A Wound That Yahweh Will Heal

verses.text: “At that time,” Yahweh announces, “I will be the God of every family of Israel, and they will be My people.”

Yahweh says:
“Those who escaped the sword
found favor out in the desert.
Israel went to look for a place to rest.”{a}

Once more I will construct you, and you will stand rebuilt,
young Israel!
You will pick up your tambourines again
and join the dancing of happy people.

You will plant vineyards again
on the hills of Samaria.
The farmers who plant them
will eat their fruit.

A day is coming when guards will shout
on the hills of Ephraim,
‘Get up! Off to Zion,
to Yahweh our God!’”

Yahweh says:
“Sing with joy for Jacob!
Shout for the greatest of the nations!
Announce it, praise Me, and say,
‘Yahweh, save Your people,
the ones left alive in Israel!’

Look, I am bringing them home from the northern land.
I am collecting them from the farthest corners of the earth.
Blind people and lame people will be among them,
and so will expecting mothers and women giving birth.
A huge crowd will come back here.

They will come crying.
I will guide them while they pray.
I will walk them along streams of water,
on a smooth road where nobody trips.
To Israel I am a father,
and Ephraim is My oldest son.”

“Nations, hear Yahweh’s message!
Tell it on faraway coasts.
Say, ‘He who scattered Israel will collect His people.
He will guard them the way a shepherd guards his flock.’

Yahweh has bought Jacob’s freedom.
He has set him free from a hand too strong for him.

They will arrive and sing on Zion’s heights.
They will flow toward Yahweh’s good gifts:
grain, fresh wine, and olive oil,
and young sheep and cattle.
Their lives will be like a garden with plenty of water,
and they will never weaken again.

Then young women will dance for joy,
and young and old men will dance with them.
I will turn their sadness into gladness.
I will comfort them and give them happiness instead of grief.

I will fill the priests with plenty.
My people will have all they need from My goodness,” Yahweh announces.

Yahweh says:
“Listen, sobbing in Ramah!
Bitter crying fills the air.
It is Rachel{c} weeping for her children.
She will not accept comfort for them,
because they are gone.”

Yahweh says:
“Stop your crying.
Wipe the tears from your eyes.
Your work will be rewarded,” Yahweh announces.
“They will come home from the land of the enemy.

You have a hope for the days ahead,” Yahweh announces.
“Your sons and daughters will return to their own land.”

“I have clearly heard Ephraim moaning,
‘You corrected me, and I learned my lesson,
like a young bull that had not been trained to pull.
Take me back, so that I can return,
because You are Yahweh my God.

After I turned away, I was sorry.
After I understood, I struck my chest in grief.
I was ashamed and embarrassed,
because I still carried the disgrace of my young days.’

Is Ephraim My precious son?
Is he a child I enjoy?
Every time I speak against him,
I still remember him.
So My heart aches for him.
I will certainly show him pity,” Yahweh announces.

“Set up road markers for yourself.
Put up signposts.
Keep the highway in mind,
the way you took when you left.
Come back, young Israel.
Come back home to your towns.

How long will you go back and forth,
unfaithful daughter?
Yahweh is creating a new thing on earth:
a woman will surround a man.”{d}

Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: “When I restore their fortunes, in Judah’s land and its towns people will say this again:
‘May Yahweh bless you, home of what is right,
holy mountain!’
Judah and every town in it will settle there together. Farmers will live there, and so will those who travel with their flocks.
I will refresh the tired and fill up everyone who is weak.”
With that, I woke up and looked about me. My sleep had been sweet.{e}
“Listen, days are coming,” Yahweh announces. “I will fill the families of Israel and Judah with people and with animals, like seed scattered on a field.
I watched over them once to pull up and tear down, to wreck and destroy, and to bring harm. This time I will watch over them to build and to plant,” Yahweh announces.

“In those days people will stop saying,
‘The parents ate sour grapes,
and the children’s teeth feel the sting.’
Rather, a person will die for his own sin. The one who eats sour grapes will be the one whose teeth feel the sting.”
“Listen, days are coming,” Yahweh announces, “when I will make a new agreement{f} with the families of Israel and Judah.
This agreement will be unlike the one I made with their ancestors the day I held their hands and led them out of Egypt. They broke it, although I was their Master,{g}” Yahweh announces.

“This is the agreement I will make with Israel’s family after those days,” Yahweh announces. “I will place My teaching{h} deep within them and write it on their hearts. Then I will be their God, and they will be My people.

Nobody will have to teach a neighbor or a brother to know Yahweh, because all of them will know Me, from the smallest to the biggest,” Yahweh announces. “I will forgive their guilt, and I will not remember their sin any more.”

This is the word of Yahweh,{i}
who set the sun in the sky to shine by day,
who fixed the rules for the moon and stars to shine at night,
who stirs up the sea so its waves roar.
His name is Yahweh of Armies.

“These rules will have to disappear
from My sight,” Yahweh announces.
“Only then will Israel’s children stop
being a nation before Me forever.”

Yahweh says:
“If anyone can measure the sky above,
or dig down to find the base of the earth below,
then I will turn away all Israel’s children
because of everything they have done,” Yahweh announces.
“Listen, days are coming,{j}” Yahweh announces. “Yahweh’s city will be rebuilt. It will reach from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
The measuring line will run on straight to Gareb Hill. After that it will turn toward Goah.

The entire valley where dead bodies and ashes are dumped,{k} and every field down to the Kidron Valley, reaching east to the corner of the Horse Gate, will belong to Yahweh as holy ground. It will never be uprooted or knocked down again.”

notes.text: The Hebrew of verse 2 is hard. It may be about the people who came out of Egypt. The Septuagint reads “I have found.”
So the Hebrew. The Septuagint reads “to him.”
Rachel means “ewe.” She was Jacob’s wife and the mother of Joseph and Benjamin. She was buried near Ramah (compare Genesis 35:19).
The meaning of “a woman will surround a man” is not certain, and people disagree about it.
These may be the prophet’s own words as he woke from a dream that showed him this.
Hebrew “cut a covenant,” a way of saying “make an agreement.” It may come from the custom of cutting up animals when making one.
Hebrew ba’alti, “I was husband (or master).” The Septuagint reads “and I turned away from them.”
Hebrew torah, “teaching” or “law.”
The Septuagint puts verse 37 before verses 35-36.
The written Hebrew has only “Look, days.” The word “coming” is supplied by the Hebrew margin.
Hebrew “valley of the corpses and the fat ashes,” probably the Valley of Ben-Hinnom (compare 7:31).

subheads.27: Each Person Responsible for His Own Sin

verses.text: In the tenth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, Yahweh gave Jeremiah a message. That was Nebuchadrezzar’s eighteenth year.{a}
Babylon’s army had Jerusalem surrounded at that time. Jeremiah the prophet was shut inside the guard’s yard, a part of the palace where Judah’s king lived.
King Zedekiah had put him there. The king had demanded, “Why do you keep preaching, ‘Yahweh says: This city is going to Babylon’s king, and he will capture it.
Zedekiah will not slip out of the Chaldeans’ grip. He will be delivered to Babylon’s king, and the two will speak face to face.
Babylon’s king will lead Zedekiah away. Zedekiah will remain in Babylon until I turn to him,’ Yahweh announces. ‘You may fight the Chaldeans, but you will not succeed’?”{b}
Jeremiah answered, “Yahweh sent me a message.
‘Your uncle Shallum has a son named Hanamel. He is on his way to you. He will ask, “Will you purchase my field at Anathoth? As a relative, you have the first right to redeem it.”’

My cousin Hanamel did arrive in the guard’s yard, exactly as Yahweh had said. He asked me, ‘Please purchase my field at Anathoth, in Benjamin’s territory. You have the right to redeem it and to keep it. Buy it for yourself.’ Then I knew the message had been from Yahweh.
“So I purchased the Anathoth field from my cousin Hanamel. The price I weighed out for it was about 7 ounces{c} of silver.
I wrote up the deed and signed it. I sealed it, brought in witnesses, and weighed the silver on a scale.
Then I took both copies of the purchase papers. One copy was sealed and held the terms and conditions. The other was open.

Baruch{d} received them. He was Neriah’s son, and Mahseiah was his grandfather. My cousin Hanamel watched, and so did the witnesses who had signed the deed. All the Judeans sitting in the guard’s yard saw it too.
In front of all of them I gave Baruch his orders.
‘Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Take these papers, the sealed deed and the open copy. Store them in a clay jar,{e} so that they stay in good shape for many years.
Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: One day people will buy houses, fields, and vineyards in this land again.’
“After I handed the purchase papers to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to Yahweh.
‘Oh, Lord Yahweh! You made the sky and the earth with Your great power and Your strong arm. Nothing is too hard for You.
You show faithful love to thousands of people. But You also make children suffer for the guilt their parents leave them. You are the great and mighty God. Your name is Yahweh of Armies.
Your plans are wise and Your deeds are powerful. Your eyes see everything people do. You give each person what his life has earned, the result of his actions.
In Egypt You did signs and wonders, and You still do them today in Israel and among all people. You made a name for Yourself, and it is famous today.
With signs and wonders you led Your people Israel out of Egypt. Your hand was strong, Your arm was stretched out, and the terror was great.
This land is what You gave them, the one You swore to their ancestors. It drips with milk and honey.
When they entered and took possession, they would not hear Your voice or live by Your teaching. Not one of Your commands did they follow. So You have let this whole disaster fall on them.

Look at the ramps the enemy has piled against the city to capture it! The city is falling into the hands of the Chaldeans who are attacking it, through the sword, hunger, and sickness. What You said has come true, and You can see it.
Yet You, Lord Yahweh, told me, “Buy the field with silver, and have witnesses see it.” But the Chaldeans are about to take the city!’”
Then Yahweh gave Jeremiah another message.
“I am Yahweh, the God of every living person. Could anything be too hard for Me?
So Yahweh says: I am giving this city to the Chaldeans and to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon. He will capture it.

The Chaldeans who are fighting this city will enter and light it. The houses will burn, including those where people made smoke for Baal on the roofs and poured out drinks to other gods to make Me angry.
Since their early days, Israel’s people and Judah’s people have done only evil in My sight. Israel’s people have done nothing but anger Me with the idols they made,” Yahweh announces.{f}
“From the day this city was built until today, it has made Me furious. So I will remove it from in front of Me.
All of them have done evil that angered Me: the people of Israel and Judah, along with their kings, officials, priests, and prophets, and everyone living in Judah and Jerusalem.
They showed Me their backs instead of their faces. I kept teaching them, early and often, but they would not listen or take correction.
They put their disgusting idols in the house that has My name. They made it unclean.

They built places of worship for Baal in the Ben-Hinnom Valley. There they made their sons and daughters pass through the fire for Molech.{g} I never ordered such a thing. It never even entered My mind. They did this horrible act and led Judah into sin.
“Now, here is what Yahweh, the God of Israel, says about this city. You say it ‘has been given to the king of Babylon by sword, hunger, and sickness.’
Look, I will gather My people from every country where I drove them in My anger, rage, and great fury. I will lead them back to this very spot and make them safe here.
They will be My people, and I will be their God.
I will give them a single heart and a single path to follow. They will fear Me for all time, and it will go well for them and for the children who come after them.
I will make a lasting agreement with them. I will not stop doing them good. Fear of Me will be placed inside their hearts, and they will never walk away from Me.
Doing them good will delight Me. With all My heart and soul, I will plant them securely in this land.
Yahweh says: Just as I sent all this huge disaster on these people, I will send them every good thing I have promised.
Fields will be bought in this land. You say it ‘is a wasteland, with no people or animals, and has been given to the Chaldeans.’

People will pay silver for fields. They will sign the deeds, seal them, and call in witnesses. It will happen in Benjamin’s land, around Jerusalem, in Judah’s towns, and in the hills, the foothills, and the Negev. I will restore their fortunes,” Yahweh announces.

notes.text: That is, 588-587 B.C., during the last siege of Jerusalem.
The Septuagint ends this verse “and Zedekiah will go into Babylon and live there.”
Hebrew “seventeen shekels,” about 195 grams.
Baruch means “blessed.” Neriah means “Yahweh is my lamp.” Mahseiah means “Yahweh is a safe place.” Baruch was Jeremiah’s helper and writer.
Hebrew “a vessel of clay,” the kind of jar used to store papers.
The Septuagint does not have the second half of verse 30.
Or “to the king.” Hebrew molekh, a god or a ritual of child sacrifice. The Septuagint reads “to the king.”

subheads.1: Jeremiah Is Locked in the Guard’s Yard

verses.text: Yahweh’s message came to Jeremiah a second time. He was still locked up in the guard’s yard.
“This is what Yahweh says. He is the One who makes it happen,{a} the One who forms it and fixes it in place. Yahweh is His name.
Ask Me, and I will reply. I will show you great and hidden things{b} that you do not know.
Yahweh, the God of Israel, says this about the houses of this city and the royal palaces of Judah. They are being torn down to build defenses against the enemy’s ramps and swords.

Men are coming to fight the Chaldeans, but all they will do is fill the houses{c} with corpses of those I struck down in My anger and fury. I have turned My face away from this city because of all its evil.
But look, I will give this city new health and healing. I will heal My people and show them rich peace and truth.
I will reverse the fortunes of Judah and of Israel. I will build them up as they were at the start.
I will wash them clean of all the guilt of their sins against Me. I will forgive every sin and every rebellion against Me.
This city will bring Me joy, praise, and honor before every nation on earth. They will hear of all the good I do for it. They will shake with fear and wonder at all the good and peace I give it.”

Yahweh says: “You keep saying about this place, ‘It is a wasteland, with no people or animals.’ You say it about the towns of Judah and the empty streets of Jerusalem, where no person, resident, or animal lives. But once more, sounds will be heard there.

You will hear glad voices and happy voices. You will hear the groom and the bride. You will hear people saying,
‘Give thanks to Yahweh of Armies,
for Yahweh is good.
His faithful love lasts forever!’
They will carry thank offerings into Yahweh’s house. I will reverse the fortunes of the land, so it is as it was at the start,” Yahweh says.
Yahweh of Armies says: “This place is now a wasteland with no people or animals. But in it and in all its towns, shepherds will again lead their flocks to rest in the pastures.
In the towns of the hills, the lowland, and the Negev, in Benjamin’s land, around Jerusalem, and in the towns of Judah, sheep will again walk past the hands of the person counting them,” Yahweh says.
“Listen, days are coming,” Yahweh announces,{d} “when I will do what I kindly promised for Israel’s family and Judah’s family.
When that time comes, a good Branch{e} will sprout from David’s family line. Justice and what is right will mark his rule over the land.
Then Judah will be rescued, and Jerusalem will rest secure. This will be her name: ‘Yahweh Is Our Righteousness.’{f}
Yahweh says: David will always have a man sitting on the throne of Israel’s family.
The Levite priests will always have a man in My presence to offer burnt offerings, burn grain offerings, and prepare sacrifices every day.”
Yahweh’s message came to Jeremiah.
“Yahweh says: You cannot cancel My agreement with the day and My agreement with the night, so that day and night stop coming at their times.
then My agreement with My servant David could also be broken. No son of his would rule on his throne. My agreement with the Levite priests who serve Me could be broken too.
Nobody can count the stars in the sky or measure the sand on the seashore. In the same way, the descendants of My servant David and the Levites who serve Me will become too many to count.”
Yahweh’s message came to Jeremiah.
“Did you hear what these people are saying? They say, ‘Yahweh has thrown out the two families{g} He chose.’ They look down on My people, as if My people were no longer a nation.
Yahweh says: Day and night keep their agreement with Me, and heaven and earth keep the laws I gave them. That is as certain as My promise.

Only if those failed could I throw out the descendants of Jacob and of My servant David. Only then would I stop choosing a ruler from David’s line over the children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Instead, I will restore their fortunes and take pity on them.”

notes.text: So the Hebrew, “who makes it,” that is, who makes His plan happen. The Septuagint reads “who made the earth.”
Hebrew betsurot, “fortified” or “closed off.” Some Hebrew copies read netsurot, “hidden.”
Hebrew “them,” probably the houses. The text of verses 4-5 is hard.
Verses 14-26 are not in the Septuagint. They expand the promise of 23:5-6.
Compare 23:5, where the same promise appears in slightly different words.
Hebrew Yahweh Tsidqenu. At 23:6 this name is given to the king. Here it is given to the city.
Probably Israel and Judah, though some think it means Judah and the family of David, or the royal and priestly families.

verses.text: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon was attacking Jerusalem and all its towns. His whole army was there, along with troops from every kingdom and people under his rule. At that time Yahweh gave Jeremiah a message.
“This is the word of Yahweh, the God of Israel: Visit King Zedekiah of Judah and tell him, ‘Yahweh says: Babylon’s king is about to get this city from Me, and he will set it on fire.
You will not escape his hands. You will be caught and given to him. You will look the king of Babylon in the eye and speak with him face to face. Then you will go to Babylon.
But listen to Yahweh’s promise, King Zedekiah of Judah. Yahweh says this about you: No sword will kill you.

You will die in peace. People burned spices at the funerals of your ancestors, the kings before you. They will burn spices for you too, and they will cry, “Oh, master!” I Myself have given My word,’ Yahweh announces.”
Jeremiah the prophet told King Zedekiah of Judah all this in Jerusalem.
At that time Babylon’s army was attacking Jerusalem and the towns of Judah that had not yet fallen: Lachish and Azekah.{a} Only those two were left among Judah’s walled towns.
Another message came to Jeremiah from Yahweh. This was after King Zedekiah made an agreement with everyone in Jerusalem to announce freedom{b} for the slaves.
Each person was to free his Hebrew slaves, men and women alike. No Judean was to hold another Judean in slavery.

All the officials and all the people who had joined in the agreement obeyed. Each one let his male and female slaves go free and did not keep them as slaves any more. They did as they promised and freed them.
Later they had second thoughts. They went and brought back the men and women they had freed, and forced them into slavery once more.{c}
Then Yahweh gave Jeremiah a message.
“Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: I made an agreement with your ancestors the day I led them out of Egypt, out of the land where they were slaves. I told them,

‘Every seventh year,{d} release any fellow Hebrew who has been sold to you. After he has worked for you six years, you must let him go free.’ But your ancestors would not listen to Me or pay attention.
Today you turned around and did what pleases Me. Each of you declared freedom for his neighbor. You made this promise in front of Me, in the house that bears My name.
But then you turned around again and disgraced My name. Each of you grabbed back the slaves you had let go to live as they wished. You made them your slaves again.

So Yahweh says: You did not obey Me. You did not announce freedom, each to his brother and neighbor. Now I announce freedom for you,” Yahweh announces. “It is freedom to die by sword, sickness, and hunger.{e} I will make you a horror to every kingdom on earth.
The men broke My agreement. They did not carry out the vow they made before Me. They walked between the halves of a calf they had cut in two, and I will make them like that calf.{f}
The officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the palace staff, the priests, and every landowner who walked between the pieces of the calf,
I will give to their enemies, who are looking for a chance to kill them. Birds of the sky and wild animals will eat their bodies.
I will also give King Zedekiah of Judah and his officials to enemies who want them dead. The army of Babylon’s king, which has pulled away from you, will get them.{g}

Listen, I am giving the order,” Yahweh announces. “I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, capture it, and burn it. I will turn the towns of Judah into a wasteland where nobody lives.”

notes.text: Lachish and Azekah were fort towns in the Judean foothills, southwest of Jerusalem. Letters on pottery pieces found at Lachish tell about this time.
Hebrew deror, “release” or “freedom.” It is the word used for the Jubilee in Leviticus 25:10.
The Septuagint shortens verses 10-11.
So the Hebrew, which counts the first year too (compare Deuteronomy 15:1, 12). The Septuagint reads “When six years end.”
The Hebrew plays on deror, “freedom.” Those who would not free their slaves are “freed” to die.
The Hebrew does not have “like.” The comparison is understood. The custom was to pass between the halves of an animal when making an agreement.
The Babylonian army had paused its siege for a while when an Egyptian army came near (37:5).

subheads.8: Slaves Set Free, Then Taken Back

verses.text: While Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, Yahweh gave Jeremiah a message.
“Go to the Rechabite family.{a} Talk with them. Bring them to Yahweh’s house, into one of the side rooms, and offer them wine.”
So I went and got Jaazaniah,{b} who was Jeremiah’s son and the grandson of Habazziniah. His brothers and all his sons came along, and so did everyone in the Rechabite family.

I led them into Yahweh’s house, to the room of the sons of Hanan, whose father was Igdaliah. Hanan was a prophet of God. The room was beside the officials’ room. It sat over the room of the doorkeeper, Maaseiah son of Shallum.
There I put out full bowls of wine and some cups in front of the Rechabites. I told them, “Have some wine.”
They replied, “We do not drink wine. Jonadab{c} son of Rechab, our ancestor, gave us a command: ‘Wine is forbidden to you and to your children, forever.
Never build a house. Never plant seed or own a vineyard. Live in tents your whole lives, so you will live long in the land where you are guests.’
We have done all that Jonadab son of Rechab told us. We have never had a drop of wine, and neither have our wives, sons, or daughters.
We have not put up houses to live in. We have no vineyard, field, or crops.
Tents are our homes. We have obeyed every command of our ancestor Jonadab.
But when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon invaded the land, we said, ‘Let’s run to Jerusalem and hide from the Chaldean and Aramean armies.’ So now we live in Jerusalem.”
Then Yahweh gave Jeremiah a message.
“Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Go and ask the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem, ‘Will you never learn a lesson and listen to Me?’ asks Yahweh.

The order of Jonadab son of Rechab to his descendants was to avoid wine, and they have kept it. Even now they drink none, because they respect their ancestor’s order. But I have talked to you early and often, and you have not listened to Me.

Over and over I sent My servants the prophets. They urged, ‘Each of you, give up your wicked ways. Do good. Quit following other gods and serving them. Then this land, which I gave you and your ancestors, will stay yours.’ But you never paid attention or listened.
The descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab have followed their ancestor’s order. But these people have not listened to Me.

So Yahweh, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Every disaster I announced against Judah and everyone in Jerusalem is about to arrive. I spoke to them, and they refused to listen. I called out, and they refused to answer.”
Jeremiah then said to the Rechabites, “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You obeyed your ancestor Jonadab’s order. You kept all his rules and did everything he told you.
So Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Jonadab son of Rechab will always have a descendant who serves Me.”{d}

notes.text: The Rechabites were a clan that came from Jonadab son of Rechab (verse 6). They lived a wandering life, with no houses, fields, or vineyards.
Jaazaniah means “Yahweh listens.” The Septuagint calls him “Jechonias son of Jeremin.”
Jonadab (also Jehonadab) means “Yahweh is generous.” He helped Jehu wipe out Baal worship (2 Kings 10:15-23).
To “stand before” Yahweh is the way to say “serve” Him. The Septuagint adds “before My face all the days.”

verses.text: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah,{a} Yahweh gave Jeremiah this message.

“Get a scroll{b} and write down all that I have said to you about Israel, Judah, and every other nation. Begin with the first time I spoke to you, back when Josiah was king, and continue through today.
Perhaps Judah’s people will learn what harm I plan to do to them. Then each of them may leave his evil road, and I will pardon their guilt and sin.”
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah. Jeremiah spoke,{c} and Baruch wrote on a scroll every word that Yahweh had told him.
Then Jeremiah gave Baruch these orders: “I am not allowed{d} to go into Yahweh’s house.

So you must go. When the people fast, read from the scroll the words you took down from my speaking. Let everyone in Yahweh’s house hear Yahweh’s words. Read them as well to the Judeans arriving from their own towns.
Perhaps they will plead for Yahweh’s mercy, and each one will leave his evil road. Yahweh has threatened these people with great anger and fury.”
Baruch son of Neriah followed all of Jeremiah the prophet’s instructions. Inside Yahweh’s house he read Yahweh’s words from the book.

It was the fifth year{e} of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month (November–December).{f} Everyone living in Jerusalem, and everyone who had come in from Judah’s towns, called a fast before Yahweh.

Then, with all the people listening, Baruch read Jeremiah’s words from the scroll in Yahweh’s house. He stood in the room of the secretary Gemariah, Shaphan’s son. It was in the upper yard, near the entrance of Yahweh’s New Gate.
Micaiah son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, heard every word of Yahweh read from the book.

He hurried down to the royal palace and into the secretary’s room. Seated there were Elishama, the secretary; Delaiah, who was Shemaiah’s son; Elnathan, Achbor’s son; Gemariah, Shaphan’s son; Zedekiah, the son of Hananiah; and the other officials.
Micaiah told them everything he remembered from Baruch’s reading to the crowd.

The officials sent Jehudi to find Baruch. Jehudi’s father was Nethaniah, his grandfather was Shelemiah, and his great-grandfather was Cushi. Jehudi said, “Bring the scroll you read to the people, and come.” Baruch son of Neriah picked up the scroll and went to them.
They said, “Sit down, please, and let us hear it.” So Baruch read it aloud.
When they had heard all of it, they were afraid and turned to look at each other. Then they said to Baruch, “The king has to be told about this.”
They questioned Baruch further: “How did you write all this? Tell us. Did Jeremiah dictate it?”
Baruch answered, “He spoke every word to me with his own mouth, and I wrote them in ink on the scroll.”
The officials then said to Baruch, “Go, you and Jeremiah, and hide. Tell no one your hiding place.”
They put the scroll away in Elishama the secretary’s room. Next they went to the king in his court and gave him the whole report.
The king sent Jehudi for the scroll. Jehudi fetched it from Elishama’s room. Then he read it out to the king and to every official standing near him.
It was the ninth month (in November–December).{g} The king sat in his winter house. A fire was burning in a pot of coals in front of him.
Whenever Jehudi finished three or four columns,{h} the king snipped them off with a scribe’s knife and dropped them into the fire. This went on until nothing was left of the scroll.
The king and his servants heard all these words, but they were not afraid. Nobody tore his clothes in sorrow.
Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah begged the king, “Please do not burn the scroll.” He would not listen to them.{i}

The king gave an order to three men: Jerahmeel, who was a royal prince; Seraiah, Azriel’s son; and Shelemiah, Abdeel’s son. They were to take Baruch the secretary and Jeremiah the prophet into custody. But Yahweh kept them hidden.
After the king burned the scroll with the words Jeremiah had spoken and Baruch had written, Yahweh gave Jeremiah another message.
“Take another scroll. Put on it every word that was written on the first one, the scroll that King Jehoiakim of Judah burned.
Then say to Jehoiakim king of Judah, ‘Yahweh says: You burned that scroll. You asked, “How dare you write that the king of Babylon is sure to come, wreck this land, and kill its people and animals?”
